symbols.doc: Token-based APNs credentials (a .p8 key from the Apple Developer portal).
symbols.docFull: Token-based APNs credentials (a `.p8` key from the Apple Developer portal).

members.name: keyId
members.doc: The key's 10-character Key ID.

members.name: teamId
members.doc: Your 10-character Team ID.

members.name: p8
members.doc: The `.p8` file's contents (a PKCS#8 `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` PEM).

members.name: topic
members.doc: The app's bundle id (the `apns-topic`).

members.name: production
members.doc:
`true` sends to `api.push.apple.com` (TestFlight / App Store builds); default `false` sends
to `api.sandbox.push.apple.com` (development builds, `aps-environment: development`).

symbols.name: AppConfig
symbols.doc: Configuration for createApp: how to resolve the route manifest and load modules, plus optional cross-cutting behavior (request logging, per-request timeout, and the rest). ServeOptions extends this for the higher-level serve entry point.
symbols.docFull:
Configuration for {@linkcode createApp}: how to resolve the route manifest and
load modules, plus optional cross-cutting behavior (request logging, per-request
timeout, and the rest). {@linkcode ServeOptions} extends this for the
higher-level {@linkcode serve} entry point.

members.name: getManifest
members.doc: Resolve the current route manifest (re-scanned per request in dev).

members.name: load
members.doc: Load a route/layout/api module by file path.

members.name: tagLoad
members.doc:
Optional loader used ONLY to tag `"use client"` boundaries as client references,
when it must differ from {@link load} to preserve ES-module-singleton identity with
the modules a page transitively imports at render (the dev loader adds a per-generation
cache-bust query to {@link load} that relative imports don't carry). Defaults to
{@link load}; prod/export leave it unset.

members.name: tagScope
members.doc:
The scope client-reference tagging is done once per (default: once per process). Dev
returns the rendered request's target (`web`, `ios`, …): each target's loader yields its
own island instances (its platform files), and each must be tagged. Server references
tagged at render register under the same scope (see {@link actionScope}).

members.name: actionScope
members.doc:
Dev: called before a Server Action dispatches; brings the request's target's registrations
up to date and returns the registry scope its actions run from (consulted before the global
one). Production leaves it unset: one global registry.

members.name: publicDir
members.doc: Directory of static assets served at the URL root.

members.name: emittedDir
members.doc:
Directory of the files plugin build steps published with `emitFile` at `denext build`
(`<outDir>/emitted`), served at the URL root ahead of {@link publicDir} (an emitted file
replaces a same-named public one, as it does in an export).

members.name: clientEntryFor
members.doc: Per-route browser bundle URL; when it returns a URL, hydration is enabled.

members.name: flightBootEntry
members.doc:
The Flight entry's deferred boot URL (`flight-boot.js`), when the build wrote one: a Flight
page whose only client code is deferred islands loads it in place of its client entry.

members.name: globalErrorEntry
members.doc:
Browser bundle URL for `global-error.tsx` (a single root file, so a plain URL rather than
a per-route resolver). When set, `renderGlobalError` hydrates the global-error document so
its `reset` and any author interactivity work; when unset, global-error is server-rendered
only (its `reset` is inert), the pre-hydration behavior.

members.name: styleHrefsFor
members.doc: Per-route stylesheet URLs (extracted CSS) linked in the document `<head>`.

members.name: matchExternal
members.signature: matchExternal?: (request: Request) => Response | null | Promise<Response | null>
members.doc:
Optional plugin claim-hook (e.g. a Pages Router). Called for a request the
core App Router did not match, right before static-asset serving and the 404.
Returns a {@linkcode Response} to serve it, or `null` to let denext fall
through. Wired from the registered plugins (see {@linkcode getPluginRequestHandler}).

members.name: devScript
members.doc: Inline script injected before </body> (dev live-reload, etc.).

members.name: devScriptSrc
members.doc:
URL of an external same-origin dev script injected before `</body>` (dev
live-reload). Preferred over {@link devScript}: an external `<script src>` is
CSP-clean under `script-src 'self'`, whereas an inline script is blocked.

members.name: getMiddleware
members.doc: Optional root middleware runner (from middleware.ts / proxy.ts).

members.name: onError
members.signature: onError?: (error: unknown, request: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>
members.doc: Custom error renderer; defaults to a plain 500.

members.name: onRequestError
members.doc:
Report a server-side request error (from a project's `instrumentation.ts`
`onRequestError`). Called once per error, before {@link onError} renders the
response. Invoked defensively — a throw from it is logged, not propagated.

members.name: onRequest
members.doc:
Opt-in per-request observability: called once after every response with the
method, path, final status, and duration. Errors thrown by it are swallowed
(observability must never break the response). A default logger emitting one
line per request is used instead when the `DENEXT_LOG` env var is set. Under
`denext start`/`dev` this is the project's `instrumentation.ts` `onRequest` export.

members.name: requestTimeout
members.doc:
Abort a request that runs longer than this many milliseconds, responding
503. The per-request {@link RequestContext} abort signal fires so cooperative
work (e.g. `fetch(url, { signal })`) can cancel. Bounds a buffered render or a
server action that hangs (e.g. a request-driven unbounded loop). The deadline stays
armed across a streamed body (a hole that never settles ends the stream with its
fallback in place). **Default: 30 000 ms**; `0` disables it (a slow request body is
always bounded separately). `denext start`/`dev` take it from the config's
`requestTimeout` (or `DENEXT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`).

members.name: maxConcurrency
members.doc:
Opt-in in-process concurrency ceiling: the max number of client requests this
instance handles at once. When set (> 0), a request arriving while that many
are already in flight is **shed immediately** with a `503` + `Retry-After`
(fast-fail, never queued) so a single instance can self-protect against
overload. A slot is held from arrival until the response is **produced** —
i.e. it bounds render/handler concurrency up to the point the `Response` is
returned, released on every exit path (success, error, abort, timeout).

It does **not** hold the slot for the lifetime of a streaming body: once the
`Response` is returned, the client-read duration of a stream (SSE, a chunked
handler body, a large static file) is intentionally *not* counted against this
in-process counter — otherwise a slow-reading client could pin slots
(slowloris) and long-lived SSE would exhaust the ceiling. Bound streaming-body
concurrency and slow-client reads at the edge / load balancer (see
https://denext.dev/docs/deploy); this ceiling **complements**, it does not
replace, that.

Background ISR regeneration (an internal detached task) is exempt. Default: no
limit. `denext start`/`dev` take it from the config's `maxConcurrency` (or
`DENEXT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`).

members.name: slotBackstop
members.doc:
Backstop (ms) to force-release a held concurrency slot when {@link requestTimeout}
is disabled (`0`). Only relevant with `maxConcurrency > 0 && requestTimeout === 0`:
without a request deadline, a render that never settles would hold its slot
forever and could eventually wedge the whole ceiling to 503s. The backstop frees
**only the slot** after this many ms (it does not abort the render — the operator
opted out of timing requests out). Default: 120000 (2 min). `denext start`/`dev` take
it from the config's `slotBackstop`.

members.name: i18n
members.doc: Optional i18n config enabling optional-prefix locale routing.

members.name: basePath
members.doc: Serve the app under a sub-path (from `denext.config` `basePath`).

members.name: trailingSlash
members.doc: Enforce a trailing slash on page URLs (from `denext.config` `trailingSlash`).

members.name: redirects
members.doc: Declarative redirect rules (from `denext.config` `redirects()`).

members.name: rewrites
members.doc: Declarative rewrite rules (from `denext.config` `rewrites()`).

members.name: headerRules
members.doc: Declarative response-header rules (from `denext.config` `headers()`).

members.name: pageCache
members.doc: Optional rendered-page cache enabling ISR (typically the prod server).

members.name: cacheKeyParams
members.doc:
Opt-in allowlist of query-parameter names that participate in the ISR page
cache key. When set, only these params fork a cached render; every other param
is ignored for keying — so high-cardinality junk (`?utm_*`, `?fbclid`, a random
cache-buster) can't multiply entries or thrash the LRU. When omitted (default),
ALL params participate, preserving existing behavior. Values still key
verbatim; only which names count is narrowed. A param not in the allowlist
still reaches the render (via `searchParams`) — it just doesn't fork the key,
so list every param whose value changes cacheable output. `denext start`/`dev` take
it from the config's `cacheKeyParams`.

members.name: cdnCacheHeaders
members.doc:
Shared-cache headers on ISR pages (`Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=…,
stale-while-revalidate=…`) — default off; `true` (or an options object) sends them. Never
on a credentialed request, a response that sets a cookie, one whose `Cache-Control` is
already set, or a request a middleware matched (unless `{ evenWithMiddleware: true }`).
`denext start`/`dev` take it from the config's `cdnCacheHeaders`.

members.name: compress
members.doc:
Compress dynamic responses per `Accept-Encoding` — default `true` (gzip, like Next.js's
`compress`); `{ encodings: ["br", "gzip"] }` also sends brotli. See `compressResponse`
(compress.ts) for the skip rules; a page/layout/route opts out with
`export const compress = false`. `denext start`/`dev` take it from the config's
`compress`.

members.name: allowedOrigins
members.doc:
Extra origins allowed to invoke Server Actions, beyond the request's own
Host (for reverse-proxy / multi-host deployments). Actions are same-origin
only by default.

members.name: actionMaxBodyBytes
members.doc:
Max Server Action request body size in bytes (default 1 MiB, matching Next.js).
Raise this only for actions that accept large payloads (e.g. multipart file
uploads). `denext start`/`dev` take it from the config's `actionMaxBodyBytes`.

members.name: apiMaxBodyBytes
members.doc:
Max request body size in bytes for `route.ts` handlers (default 1 MiB). A route raises
or lifts its own cap with `export const maxBodyBytes = N | false`. An over-cap body is a
413 before the handler runs (declared `Content-Length`) or errors the body stream as
the handler reads it.

members.name: apiBatch
members.doc: Limits for the typed-API batch endpoint (`POST /_denext/api-batch`).

members.name: cors
members.doc:
Cross-origin access to route handlers and the native auth endpoints (the config's `cors`).
Validated when `createApp` runs: a malformed or `"null"` origin, or `"*"` with credentials,
throws there. Unset → no CORS headers. See `src/server/cors.ts`.

members.name: appLinks
members.doc:
The universal link / App Link association files (the config's `appLinks`), answered before
any redirect or middleware. Unset → neither file is served. See `src/server/app-links.ts`.

members.name: canonicalOrigin
members.doc:
An explicit public origin (e.g. `"https://example.com"`) used to build
absolute URLs (auto-populated `og:image`, canonical). Overrides request
headers — the most robust option when the origin is fixed. Also makes Server
Action origin checks scheme-strict (rejects an `http` origin for an `https` app).
`denext start`/`dev` take it from the config's `canonicalOrigin` (or
`DENEXT_CANONICAL_ORIGIN`).

members.name: trustForwardedHeaders
members.doc:
Trust `X-Forwarded-Proto`/`X-Forwarded-Host` when building absolute URLs.
Enable ONLY behind a trusted reverse proxy that sets those headers; otherwise
a client can spoof the generated origin. Ignored when {@link canonicalOrigin}
is set. Default false (forwarded headers are not trusted). `denext start`/`dev` take
it from the config's `trustForwardedHeaders` (or `DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1`).

members.name: rateLimitHeader
members.doc:
A header the fronting proxy sets to the client address (`cf-connecting-ip`,
`fly-client-ip`, `x-real-ip`) that per-address limits key on — `rateLimit()`,
`denextAuth`'s per-IP budgets, `live.limits.maxConnectionsPerIp` and
`clientIpForLimits()` (never `clientIp()`). A request without an IP address in it falls back
to the socket peer / trusted hop. Believed only from a trusted proxy:
a peer in {@linkcode AppConfig.rateLimitTrustedProxies}, or (none listed) a loopback/private
peer with `trustForwardedHeaders`. `denext start`/`dev` take it from the config's
`rateLimitHeader` (or `DENEXT_RATE_LIMIT_HEADER`).

members.name: rateLimitTrustedProxies
members.doc:
CIDR ranges (or addresses) of the proxies whose `rateLimitHeader` is believed; a request
from any other peer keys its limits on that peer. `denext start`/`dev` take it from the
config's `rateLimitTrustedProxies` (or `DENEXT_RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXIES`).

members.name: rateLimitLocalAddresses
members.doc:
Apply per-address limits to a loopback/private socket peer too, counted by its own address,
instead of skipping them (the default, since such a peer is usually a proxy every visitor
shares). `denext start`/`dev` take it from the config's `rateLimitLocalAddresses` (or
`DENEXT_RATE_LIMIT_LOCAL_ADDRESSES=1`).

members.name: desktopAppOrigin
members.doc:
The app's own Deno Desktop origin (`desktop.app.origin`, normalized: `myapp://app`). The
same-origin checks (Server Actions, the API batch, `denextAuth`'s POSTs) accept an `Origin`
header exactly equal to it. `denext start`/`dev` take it from the config.

members.name: flight
members.doc:
Enable the Flight (`"use client"`/`"use server"`) boundary. When on (and
{@link appDir} is set), a route that involves a client module is rendered to
a Flight payload and hydrates from client islands only. Routes with no
boundary keep the isomorphic whole-tree hydration. Off by default.

members.name: appDir
members.doc: The app directory, required for stable client-reference ids under {@link flight}.

members.name: flightRoutes
members.doc:
Route paths that must render via Flight (a client island is reachable from
their import graph). Computed by the build (`computeBoundaryRoutes`). When
omitted, gating falls back to the route's own convention-module directives.

members.name: flightClients
members.doc:
The app's `"use client"` modules (client id → ref), imported and tagged once
so the renderer emits references for them. From the boundary manifest.

members.name: flightServers
members.doc:
The app's `"use server"` modules (module id → ref), imported and tagged once
so their exports auto-register and serialize as action references. From the
boundary manifest.

members.name: flightBoundary
members.doc:
The Flight boundary of the request being rendered, when it is not {@link flightRoutes} /
{@link flightClients} / {@link flightServers}: dev returns a platform session's own
boundary (its platform files may reach other `"use client"` modules), null for those.

members.name: cacheComponents
members.doc:
Enable Cache Components / Partial Prerendering (Next.js 16). When on (and a
{@link pageCache} is present), a cacheable GET renders a request-independent
static shell — cached once — with per-request dynamic holes (subtrees that
read `cookies()`/`headers()` behind a Suspense boundary) spliced in on every
request. Off by default; when off the render path is unchanged.

members.name: csp
members.doc:
App-wide Content-Security-Policy default (`denext.config` `csp`): `"strict"`
(default), `"off"` (no CSP header), or a {@link CspSetting} object of global
opt-ins. A route's own `csp` export overrides it. Absent ⇒ `"strict"`.

members.name: streaming
members.doc:
Incremental (Suspense) streaming, **on by default** (the top-level `streaming`
config); set `false` to opt out (buffer the whole document before responding). Streamed
responses carry the same strict hash-based CSP as buffered ones (the swap runtime
is a hashed constant), survive a failing Suspense boundary (its fallback stays),
and cover Flight (`"use client"`) routes via their own path. Streaming applies to
hard-navigation/initial GET renders that aren't ISR/PPR-cached (a cached shell or
a soft navigation takes its own path first); a `csp: "off"` route emits no CSP
header, as when buffered.

members.name: hsts
members.doc:
`Strict-Transport-Security` tuning (`denext.config` `hsts`): default
host-only `max-age=31536000`, opt into `includeSubDomains`/`preload`, or
`false` to omit the header.

members.name: publicEnvKeys
members.doc:
Allowlist of public-env var names to embed in each page's env island (the
build's referenced set ∪ the `publicEnv` config). When set, only these
`NEXT_PUBLIC_`/`DENEXT_PUBLIC_` vars ship to the browser instead of every
prefixed one. Undefined ⇒ ship all (dev, or no build scan).

symbols.name: apple
symbols.doc: Sign in with Apple (OIDC) over response_mode=form_post, requesting openid name email: Apple POSTs the authorization response to {basePath}/callback/apple, and returns the name (in a user form field) and email (in the id_token) only that way. The email comes from the verified id_token — often a private relay address; the name from the user field, which Apple sends on a user's FIRST sign-in only, so persist it (an adapter does).
symbols.docFull:
Sign in with Apple (OIDC) over `response_mode=form_post`, requesting `openid name email`:
Apple POSTs the authorization response to `{basePath}/callback/apple`, and returns the name
(in a `user` form field) and email (in the `id_token`) only that way. The email comes from
the verified `id_token` — often a private relay address; the name from the `user` field,
which Apple sends on a user's FIRST sign-in only, so persist it (an adapter does).

`clientSecret` must be the ES256 client-secret **JWT** you mint from your Apple key
(max 6 months); denext passes it through to the token endpoint verbatim.

params.name: options
params.doc: The app's Apple client credentials (Services ID + secret JWT).

symbols.name: AppleAppLinks
symbols.doc: The iOS side of AppLinksConfig.
symbols.docFull: The iOS side of {@link AppLinksConfig}.

members.name: appIds
members.doc:
The apps, as `<Team ID>.<bundle id>` (`ABCDE12345.com.example.app`): the Team ID from the
Apple Developer account, the bundle id from Xcode.

members.name: paths
members.doc:
The URL paths that open the app (`*` and `?` wildcards). A leading `!` excludes a path
(`"!/admin/*"`); order matters, the first match wins. Default `["*"]`: every path.

members.name: webcredentials
members.doc:
Also list the apps under `webcredentials`, so iOS offers this domain's saved passwords
and passkeys in the app. Default `true`.

symbols.name: AppleWebAppMetadata
symbols.doc: appleWebApp metadata (apple-mobile-web-app-*).
symbols.docFull: `appleWebApp` metadata (`apple-mobile-web-app-*`).

members.name: capable
members.doc: `apple-mobile-web-app-capable` (default yes).

members.name: title
members.doc: `apple-mobile-web-app-title`.

members.name: statusBarStyle
members.doc: `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style`.

members.name: startupImage
members.signature: startupImage?: string | Array<string | { url: string; media?: string }>
members.doc: `<link rel="apple-touch-startup-image">` entries.

symbols.name: AppLinksConfig
symbols.doc: The domain-association files for the app's universal links / App Links (appLinks in denext.config.ts). Pair it with denext mobile add deep-links --domain <host>.
symbols.docFull:
The domain-association files for the app's universal links / App Links (`appLinks` in
`denext.config.ts`). Pair it with `denext mobile add deep-links --domain <host>`.

members.name: apple
members.doc: Serve `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` for these iOS apps.

members.name: android
members.doc:
Serve `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` for this Android app, or for each app of a list (one
statement each: a debug and a release build, or several apps on one domain). The same
`{ packageName, sha256CertFingerprints }` objects can go to `denextAuth({ passkeys: {
androidApps } })`, which accepts their passkey origins.

symbols.name: AppLinksMetadata
symbols.signature: type AppLinksMetadata = Record<string, Record<string, string | number> | Array<Record<string, string | number>>>
symbols.doc: al:* app-link tags (Next.js appLinks); each entry is a record of al:<platform>:<key>.
symbols.docFull: `al:*` app-link tags (Next.js `appLinks`); each entry is a record of `al:<platform>:<key>`.

symbols.name: asyncProps
symbols.doc: Make value awaitable to itself without changing its enumerable shape. Idempotent.
symbols.docFull: Make `value` awaitable to itself without changing its enumerable shape. Idempotent.

symbols.name: AsyncProps
symbols.doc: A value that is both T and awaitable to T (Next 15's Promise<T> page props).
symbols.docFull: A value that is both `T` and awaitable to `T` (Next 15's `Promise<T>` page props).

symbols.name: auth
symbols.doc: Read the current request's auth session, or null when signed out. Call from a Server Component, a route.ts handler, or middleware.ts — anywhere inside the request context.
symbols.docFull:
Read the current request's auth session, or `null` when signed out. Call from a
Server Component, a `route.ts` handler, or `middleware.ts` — anywhere inside the
request context.

A session that has passed the first factor but not the second
({@link AuthSession.mfaPending}) reads as `null` here — it **fails closed**, so every
guard built on `auth()` (requireAuth, requireSession, Live `authorize`, Server
Actions) refuses it without having to know MFA exists.

With an adapter, a cookie session's user is re-read on every request (once per request,
however many times `auth()` is called): a deleted or banned user, and an SSO user (whose
identity provider never starts a denextAuth session), read as `null` from their very next
request. A bearer session's user is re-read the same way by its own verification.

symbols.name: auth0
symbols.doc: Auth0 (OIDC). Note the issuer carries Auth0's trailing slash (https://<domain>/) — that is what the tenant's discovery document and id_token declare, and iss is compared exactly.
symbols.docFull:
Auth0 (OIDC). Note the issuer carries Auth0's trailing slash
(`https://<domain>/`) — that is what the tenant's discovery document and `id_token`
declare, and `iss` is compared exactly.

params.name: options
params.doc: Tenant domain plus the app's client credentials.

symbols.name: Auth0Options
symbols.doc: Options for auth0.
symbols.docFull: Options for {@link auth0}.

members.name: domain
members.doc: The tenant domain, e.g. `"acme.eu.auth0.com"` or a custom domain. Host only.

symbols.name: AuthAdapter
symbols.signature: interface AuthAdapter extends OAuthServerAdapter, CustomProviderAdapter, Web3NonceAdapter
symbols.doc: Where denext auth persists identities. Implement it over any store; denext ships inMemoryAuthAdapter() and sqliteAuthAdapter().
symbols.docFull:
Where denext auth persists identities. Implement it over any store; denext ships
`inMemoryAuthAdapter()` and `sqliteAuthAdapter()`.

**Atomicity contract.** Three methods are **consume-once** and MUST be atomic against
concurrent callers — a compare-and-delete / conditional update inside one transaction,
not a read followed by a write. Two racing requests must see exactly one success:
{@linkcode AuthAdapter.useVerificationToken} (delete-and-return),
{@linkcode AuthAdapter.consumeBackupCode} (match-and-remove) and
{@linkcode AuthAdapter.claimMfaFactorStep} (claim a TOTP step). So are the passkey group's
{@linkcode AuthAdapter.usePasskeyChallenge} (delete-and-return),
{@linkcode AuthAdapter.createPasskey} (insert unless the ID exists) and
{@linkcode AuthAdapter.updatePasskey} (compare-and-swap on the counter). A non-atomic
implementation turns each of them into a replay window.

members.name: sessions
members.doc:
An optional {@link ./session-store.ts | SessionStore} over the same storage. It is
used only when the app asks for `session: { strategy: "database" }` (or passes
`sessionStore` itself) — an adapter never silently makes sessions stateful.

members.name: rateLimits
members.doc:
An optional {@link ./rate-limit.ts | RateLimitStore} over the same storage. The auth
limiters use it when the app runs on `@denext/backend`'s Postgres and sets no
`rateLimit.store`, so every replica counts against one budget.

members.name: createUser
members.doc: Create a user.

params.name: user
params.doc: The profile to store; supply id only to keep an externally minted one.

members.returns: The stored record, with its final id.

members.name: getUser
members.doc: Look a user up by id.

members.name: getUserByEmail
members.doc: Look a user up by email (case-insensitively, if the store can).

members.name: getUserByAccount
members.doc: Look a user up by a linked provider account — the primary sign-in path.
members.returns: The user, or undefined when the account is not linked.

members.name: updateUser
members.doc: Merge changed fields into a user.

params.name: user
params.doc: The id plus the fields to change.

members.name: getUserByPhone
members.doc:
Look a user up by phone number (optional; gates phone sign-in). Numbers are stored and
matched in E.164 form.

members.name: listUsers
members.signature: listUsers?(options: { page: number; perPage: number }): MaybePromise<{ users: AdapterUser[]; total: number }>
members.doc: One page of users, oldest first (optional; gates the admin user listing).

params.name: options
params.doc: The 1-based page and its size, perPage.

members.returns: The page and the total number of users.

members.name: linkAccount
members.doc: Link a provider account to a user.

members.name: unlinkAccount
members.doc: Unlink a provider account (optional).

members.name: listAccounts
members.doc: Every provider account linked to a user (optional).

members.name: createVerificationToken
members.doc: Store a single-use verification token.

params.name: token
params.doc: The record to store (hash only — never the presented token).

members.name: useVerificationToken
members.doc:
**Atomically** redeem a verification token: delete it and return what it was, or
return `undefined` when it is absent (already spent, or never existed). The delete
and the read MUST happen as one operation — two concurrent redemptions of the same
token must produce exactly one record. An expired token is consumed too but
resolves `undefined` (fail closed) — it is never left to be retried.

params.name: ref
params.doc: The identifier + token hash + purpose to redeem.

members.name: getCredential
members.doc: The stored password hash for a user (optional).
members.returns: The scrypt$… string, or undefined when the user has no password.

members.name: setCredential
members.doc: Set (or replace) a user's password hash (optional).

members.name: deleteCredential
members.doc:
Remove a user's password hash (optional). A pre-account-hijacking eviction uses it to retire
a password set before the address was proven; without it the hash is overwritten with one of
a random secret instead. Removing a password the user doesn't have is not an error.

members.name: createApiToken
members.doc: Store a bearer API token (optional).

members.name: getApiTokenByHash
members.doc: Look a bearer token up by the hash of the presented string (optional).

members.name: touchApiToken
members.doc: Record a successful presentation (optional; best-effort, never fails a request).

members.name: revokeApiToken
members.doc: Revoke a bearer token (optional).
members.returns: true when a token that wasn't revoked yet was revoked, false for an unknown or already revoked id. (An adapter that returns nothing is taken to have revoked it, so apiTokenRevoked fires for every call — return the boolean.)

members.name: listApiTokens
members.doc: A user's bearer tokens (optional). Implementations never return the secret.

members.name: getMfa
members.doc: A user's TOTP factor (optional).
members.returns: The record, or undefined when the user has no factor.

members.name: setMfa
members.doc: Store (or replace) a user's TOTP factor (optional).

members.name: deleteMfa
members.doc:
Remove a user's TOTP factor and backup codes (optional). `disableTotp` and the
pre-account-hijacking eviction use it; without it they write an empty, unconfirmed record,
which reads as "not enrolled" everywhere. Removing a factor the user doesn't have is not an
error.

members.name: replaceMfaSecret
members.signature: replaceMfaSecret?(userId: string, expected: string, next: string): MaybePromise<boolean>
members.doc:
**Atomically** replace a user's stored TOTP secret, only while it still equals
`expected` (optional) — how a pre-4.0 record's secret is cleared once it has moved into a
factor. A compare-and-swap of that one field, never a whole-record write: a concurrent
`consumeBackupCode` must not be undone. Without it the move falls back to `setMfa`.

params.name: expected
params.doc: The stored secret as it was read.

members.returns: true when the secret was replaced; false when it had changed meanwhile.

members.name: consumeBackupCode
members.signature: consumeBackupCode?(userId: string, matches: (hash: string) => MaybePromise<boolean>): MaybePromise<boolean>
members.doc:
**Atomically** spend one backup code. Backup codes are stored salted-and-hashed, so
the adapter cannot look one up by value: it walks
{@linkcode MfaRecord.backupCodeHashes}, `await`s `matches(hash)` for each, and — still
inside the same transaction / critical section — removes the first hash that matches
and reports `true`. Two concurrent redemptions of the same code must yield exactly
one `true`.

params.name: matches
params.doc: Constant-time comparison of the presented code against one stored hash.

members.returns: true when a code was matched AND removed.

members.name: claimTotpStep
members.doc:
**Atomically** claim a TOTP time step, the replay guard for a valid code presented
twice. Succeeds only when `step` is strictly greater than the stored
{@linkcode MfaRecord.lastStep}, and stores it in the same operation. Two concurrent
presentations of one code must yield exactly one `true`.

params.name: step
params.doc: The TOTP step the presented code verified against.

members.returns: true when the step was claimed (i.e. not a replay).

members.name: createMfaFactor
members.doc: Store a new factor (optional; the factor group gates `/auth/v1/factors`).

members.name: listMfaFactors
members.doc: A user's factors, oldest first.

members.name: updateMfaFactor
members.doc:
Change a factor's status, label, secret (a re-sealed TOTP secret, a WebAuthn factor's
credential id) or challenge time.

members.name: claimMfaFactorStep
members.doc:
**Atomically** claim a TOTP step on a factor: succeeds only when `step` is greater than its
stored `lastStep`, and stores it in the same operation (the replay guard).

params.name: step
params.doc: The step the presented code verified against.

members.name: deleteMfaFactor
members.doc: Remove a factor. Removing an unknown one is not an error.

members.name: createNativeGrant
members.doc:
Store a single-use native grant (a code or a nonce) — hash only (optional; the native
session group gates `denextAuth({ native })`).

members.name: useNativeGrant
members.signature: useNativeGrant?(hash: string, kind: NativeGrantRecord["kind"]): MaybePromise<NativeGrantRecord | undefined>
members.doc:
**Atomically** redeem a native grant: delete it and return what it was, or `undefined`
when absent. Two concurrent redemptions must produce exactly one record. An expired grant
is consumed too but resolves `undefined` (fail closed).

params.name: kind
params.doc: The grant kind the caller expects (a code can never redeem as a nonce).

members.name: createNativeSession
members.doc: Store a new native session family.

members.name: getNativeSession
members.doc:
A native session family by id, exactly as stored (revoked and expired ones included — the
caller decides; reuse detection needs to see a revoked family).

members.name: rotateNativeSession
members.signature: rotateNativeSession?(id: string, fromGeneration: number, expiresAt: number, rotation?: { rotatedAt: number }): MaybePromise<boolean>
members.doc:
**Atomically** advance a family from `fromGeneration` to `fromGeneration + 1` — a
compare-and-swap that succeeds only while the stored generation is still `fromGeneration`
and the family is not revoked. Two concurrent refreshes with one token yield exactly one
`true`. The same write stores `rotation.rotatedAt` as
{@linkcode NativeSessionRecord.rotatedAt}.

params.name: fromGeneration
params.doc: The generation the presented refresh token carries.

params.name: expiresAt
params.doc: The family's new expiry, epoch seconds.

members.returns: true when this call advanced the generation.

members.name: revokeNativeSession
members.doc:
Revoke one family (sign-out, or refresh-token reuse). Revoking an unknown or already
revoked family is a no-op.

members.name: revokeNativeSessionsByUser
members.doc:
Revoke every family of a user ("sign out everywhere", password reset) — except `exceptId`,
when given ("sign out my other sessions").

members.name: createPasskey
members.doc:
Store a newly registered passkey (optional; the passkey group gates
`denextAuth({ passkeys })`). **Atomic** against a duplicate ID: when a credential with
this `id` is already registered — to anyone — store nothing and return `false`
(WebAuthn L3 §7.1 step 25).
members.returns: true when stored, false when the ID was taken.

members.name: getPasskey
members.doc: A passkey by credential ID.

members.name: listPasskeys
members.doc: A user's passkeys, oldest first.

members.name: updatePasskey
members.signature: updatePasskey?(id: string, fromSignCount: number, update: { signCount: number; backedUp: boolean; lastUsedAt: number }): MaybePromise<boolean>
members.doc:
**Atomically** record a verified assertion: a compare-and-swap that writes `update` only
while the stored `signCount` is still `fromSignCount`, so two assertions racing on one
counter value can't both pass the clone check.

params.name: fromSignCount
params.doc: The counter the assertion was verified against.

params.name: update
params.doc: The new counter, backup state and last-use time.

members.returns: true when this call wrote the update.

members.name: deletePasskey
members.doc: Remove a passkey. Removing an unknown one is not an error.

members.name: createPasskeyChallenge
members.doc: Store a single-use WebAuthn challenge.

params.name: record
params.doc: The challenge's hash, expiry and ceremony.

members.name: usePasskeyChallenge
members.doc:
**Atomically** redeem a challenge: delete it and return what it was, or `undefined` when
absent. Two concurrent redemptions must produce exactly one record; an expired one is
consumed too but resolves `undefined`.

members.name: createSsoProvider
members.doc:
Store a new SSO provider and its domains, **atomically** refusing a duplicate entity id or
a domain another provider holds (optional; the group gates `/auth/v1/admin/sso/providers`).
members.returns: ok, entity_id_exists or domain_exists (nothing stored then).

members.name: updateSsoProvider
members.doc: Replace a stored provider (and its domains) by id, with the same uniqueness rules.

params.name: record
params.doc: The provider as it should now be.

members.returns: ok, not_found, entity_id_exists or domain_exists (nothing changed then).

members.name: getSsoProvider
members.doc: A provider by id.

members.name: getSsoProviderByEntityId
members.doc: The provider with this entity id.

members.name: getSsoProviderByDomain
members.doc: The provider a domain routes to.

members.name: listSsoProviders
members.doc: Every stored provider, oldest first.

members.name: deleteSsoProvider
members.doc: Remove a provider, its domains and its SSO session records.
members.returns: true when a provider was removed.

members.name: createSsoSession
members.doc: Record the SSO origin of a session family (and drop expired records).

params.name: record
params.doc: The session's provider, NameID and SessionIndex.

members.name: listSsoSessions
members.doc: The unexpired session records of one NameID at one provider.

members.name: claimSamlMessageId
members.doc:
**Atomically** claim a SAML message id (an assertion or logout message ID, namespaced by
the caller): `true` the first time, `false` for every later claim while it is kept. Kept at
least until `expiresAt` (epoch seconds) — the replay cache every replica shares.

params.name: expiresAt
params.doc: Until when it must be remembered.

members.name: recordSsoSessionIndex
members.signature: recordSsoSessionIndex?(providerId: string, nameId: string, sessionIndex: string | undefined, sid: string, expiresAt: number): MaybePromise<void>
members.doc:
Record that a SAML sign-in at `providerId` started the cookie session `sid` (and prune
expired index rows).

params.name: sessionIndex
params.doc: Its SessionIndex, or undefined when it gave none.

params.name: expiresAt
params.doc: When the session ends (its absolute ceiling), epoch seconds.

members.name: listSsoSessionIndexBySessionIndex
members.signature: listSsoSessionIndexBySessionIndex?(providerId: string, nameId: string, sessionIndex: string): MaybePromise<SsoSessionIndexRecord[]>
members.doc: The unexpired cookie sessions one SessionIndex of a NameID started.

members.name: listSsoSessionIndexByNameId
members.doc: The unexpired cookie sessions a NameID started, every SessionIndex.

members.name: revokeSids
members.signature: revokeSids?(sids: readonly string[], expiresAt: number): MaybePromise<void>
members.doc:
Put cookie sessions on the revocation list until `expiresAt` (and prune expired entries).
Never evicted early.

params.name: expiresAt
params.doc: Until when they stay revoked, epoch seconds.

members.name: isSidRevoked
members.doc: Whether the cookie session `sid` is on the revocation list (and not expired).

members.name: deleteUser
members.doc:
Delete a user and everything keyed by them: linked accounts, the password hash, bearer
API tokens, the MFA factor, native session families, and verification tokens issued to
their address (optional; gates `POST {basePath}/account/delete`). Deleting an unknown user
is not an error.

members.name: close
members.doc: Optional: release resources (a database handle) when the server drains.

symbols.name: AuthCallbacks
symbols.doc: Callbacks that let an app veto or enrich a sign-in.
symbols.docFull: Callbacks that let an app veto or enrich a sign-in.

members.name: signIn
members.signature: signIn?: (user: AuthUser, provider: string) => Promise<boolean | AuthUser> | boolean | AuthUser
members.doc: Return false to deny a sign-in, or a modified user to enrich the session.

members.name: session
members.doc: Adjust the session payload before it is issued.

members.name: authorized
members.signature: authorized?: (input: AuthorizedCallbackInput) => Promise<boolean | Response> | boolean | Response
members.doc:
The authorization hook `requireAuth` consults once a live session exists — richer
than `role`, because it sees the request. Return `true` to allow, `false` to refuse
exactly as an unauthenticated request is refused (a redirect to the sign-in page
carrying `callbackUrl`), or your own `Response` (a 403 page, a JSON envelope) to have
it returned verbatim.

symbols.name: AuthConfig
symbols.doc: Configuration for denextAuth.
symbols.docFull: Configuration for {@link ../auth/mod.ts | denextAuth}.

members.name: providers
members.doc: Configured providers.

members.name: secret
members.doc:
HMAC signing secret(s) for the session cookie (rotate with an array). At least 32
chars: shorter warns in development and makes `denextAuth()` throw in production.

members.name: canonicalOrigin
members.doc:
The app's canonical origin (e.g. `https://example.com`). REQUIRED in production
so the OAuth `redirect_uri` is byte-stable and immune to Host-header injection.

members.name: trustForwardedHeaders
members.doc:
The app runs behind a proxy/load balancer that sets `x-forwarded-for`, so every
per-IP rate-limit budget (and `signInFailed`'s `ip`) may key on that header's LAST hop
(the one the proxy appended). Off by default — without a proxy the header is
attacker-controlled, and the limiters key on the socket peer instead. **Unset, it
inherits the app-level `trustForwardedHeaders` / `DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1`**, so the auth
limiters and `clientIp()` agree on the client; set it only to override the app for auth.

members.name: callbacks
members.doc: Optional sign-in/session callbacks.

members.name: maxAge
members.doc: Session lifetime in seconds (default 7 days).

members.name: pages
members.signature: pages?: { signIn?: string; afterSignIn?: string; afterSignOut?: string; mfa?: string; verifyRequest?: string; error?: string }
members.doc: Where to send the user after sign-in / sign-out when no `callbackUrl` is given.

members.name: dangerouslyAllowInsecureProviders
members.doc:
DANGEROUS: permit `http://localhost` providers in development (bypasses the
SSRF localhost block for token/userinfo/jwks). Never enable in production.

members.name: rateLimit
members.doc:
Brute-force protection. ON by default, with five budgets that each answer a generic `429`:
credentials, 5 failed attempts per client IP + identifier per 15 minutes; sign-in starts
(`/signin/*`), 100 per client IP per 15 minutes (`rateLimit.signin`); session reads
(`GET /session`), 300 per client IP per minute (`rateLimit.session`); emailed tokens
(verification, reset, magic link, one-time code), 3 sends per address per 15 minutes
(`rateLimit.verification`); second factors, 5 attempts per user per 5 minutes
(`rateLimit.mfa`).
Tune the limits, key, or store here, or pass `false` to disable every limiter (e.g. you
rate-limit at the edge). The default store is per-process — pass a shared `store` for
multi-replica deployments.

members.name: sessionStore
members.doc:
Opt in to **server-side, revocable sessions**. When set, the cookie carries only a
random session id and the payload lives in the store, so `revokeSession` /
`revokeAllSessions` end sessions immediately (a stolen cookie, a password change).
When unset (the default) sessions are stateless signed cookies — zero-config and
multi-replica-safe, but only expiry can end them. See `inMemorySessionStore` /
`sqliteSessionStore`, and note a per-process store isn't shared across replicas.

members.name: adapter
members.doc:
Where users, linked accounts, credentials, verification tokens, API tokens and MFA
factors are persisted. Optional: without one, denext stays the stateless
OAuth/Credentials layer it has always been and `session.user.id` is whatever the
provider's `profile` mapper returned. **With** one, sign-in resolves (or creates) an
adapter user and `session.user.id` becomes that adapter id. An adapter does **not**
make sessions stateful — see {@link AuthSessionConfig.strategy}.

members.name: session
members.doc: Session lifetime, sliding refresh, and cookie-vs-database storage.

members.name: basePath
members.doc:
Mount the endpoints under this prefix instead of `/auth` (e.g. `"/account/auth"`).
A leading slash is added and a trailing one stripped; `"/"` is refused, because the
handler would then claim every request.

members.name: cookies
members.doc: Override the session / OAuth-transaction cookie names and attributes.

members.name: events
members.doc: Lifecycle hooks (sign-in, sign-out, failures, revocation, user/account creation).

members.name: logger
members.doc: Where the framework logs. Silent by default — auth never writes to the console.

members.name: hasher
members.doc:
How user-supplied secrets (Credentials passwords, MFA backup codes) are hashed and
checked. Defaults to `scryptHasher()`.

members.name: sendVerificationRequest
members.doc:
Deliver a verification token (email verification, password reset, magic link, OTP).
`smtpMailer({ host, user, pass, from })` sends them over SMTP (TLS required); the flows
that need one refuse to start without this (or `hooks.sendEmail`).

members.name: sendSms
members.doc:
Deliver an SMS — phone sign-in codes (`phoneOtp()`), phone MFA codes and phone changes, for
denext's own endpoints and for `/auth/v1` (`backend({ supabase })`) alike. denext ships no
SMS gateway; the phone flows refuse to start without this (or `hooks.sendSms`).

members.name: captcha
members.doc:
Verify a captcha token (hCaptcha or Turnstile) on the endpoints that create sessions or
send messages — sign-up, password sign-in, one-time codes, recovery, anonymous sign-in —
on denext's endpoints and `/auth/v1` alike. Off by default. denext's endpoints (the
credentials POST, an email or phone SEND, `POST /anonymous`, `POST /reset`) read the token
from `captchaToken`, `captcha_token`, `cf-turnstile-response` or `h-captcha-response` in the
body, or the `x-captcha-token` header, and refuse without one the provider confirms
(`400 { error: "captcha_failed" }`, or a form's `303 ?error=CaptchaFailed`) before any
adapter work or rate-limit spend. Redeeming a code or link needs no token.

members.name: hooks
members.doc:
Supabase's auth hooks, shared by denext's endpoints and `/auth/v1`: `customAccessToken`
shapes the claims of every session (an `/auth/v1` access token, and the
`request.jwt.claims` a cookie session's queries run with), `sendEmail` delivers every auth
email (instead of `sendVerificationRequest`), `sendSms` every SMS (instead of `sendSms`).

members.name: anonymous
members.doc:
Anonymous sign-in: a user with no identifier yet (`POST {basePath}/anonymous`,
`supabase.auth.signInAnonymously()`), who becomes permanent by adding a confirmed email or
phone — on denext's endpoints by redeeming an email link / code or a `phoneOtp()` code for
an identifier no account has, from the anonymous session. Default `false`: the endpoint does
not exist.

members.name: email
members.doc: Token lifetimes and link targets for email verification, password reset, magic links and one-time codes.

members.name: mfa
members.doc: Second-factor (TOTP) policy.

members.name: passkeys
members.doc:
Passkeys (WebAuthn): `POST {basePath}/passkey/*` registers them from a signed-in session
and signs in with them (a first factor, or the second factor of a pending session).
Needs an adapter with the passkey group (both shipped adapters have it). `true` takes
every default. See {@link AuthPasskeyConfig}.

members.name: native
members.doc:
Native session mode for a Capacitor (or desktop) app: code exchange → bearer access token
+ rotating refresh token, and native Apple / Google `id_token` sign-in. See
{@link AuthNativeConfig}.

members.name: onAccountDeleted
members.doc:
Called after `POST {basePath}/account/delete` removed a user (and revoked their sessions
and Apple tokens) — delete the app's own rows for them here. Awaited; a throw is logged,
never shown to the caller (the account is already gone).

symbols.name: AuthCookieConfig
symbols.doc: One auth cookie's name and attributes.
symbols.docFull: One auth cookie's name and attributes.

members.name: name
members.doc:
The cookie name *before* the `__Host-` prefix. Defaults are `"denext_auth"` (session)
and `"denext_auth_tx"` (OAuth transaction) — changing one logs every existing session
of that kind out once.

members.name: hostPrefix
members.doc:
Origin-lock the cookie with the `__Host-` name prefix (Secure + `Path=/` + no
`Domain`). **On by default**, and leaving it on is strongly recommended: it is what
stops a sibling subdomain reading or shadowing the cookie. Over plain http on a loopback
host, or outside production, the prefix is left off for that request (a browser refuses
`__Host-` over http, even on `localhost`).

members.name: sameSite
members.doc: Cookie `SameSite` (default `"Lax"` — the OAuth callback is a top-level GET).

members.name: path
members.doc: Cookie `Path` (default `"/"`, and forced to `"/"` under `__Host-`).

symbols.name: AuthEmailConfig
symbols.doc: The email-token flows' knobs: how long each kind of token lives and which pages the emailed links open. Every field is optional; lifetimes are in **seconds**, and a non-finite or non-positive lifetime falls back to its default.
symbols.docFull:
The email-token flows' knobs: how long each kind of token lives and which pages the
emailed links open. Every field is optional; lifetimes are in **seconds**, and a
non-finite or non-positive lifetime falls back to its default.

members.name: verifyMaxAge
members.doc: How long an email-verification link stays valid, in seconds. Default `86400` (24 hours).

members.name: resetMaxAge
members.doc: How long a password-reset link stays valid, in seconds. Default `3600` (1 hour).

members.name: magicMaxAge
members.doc: How long a magic sign-in link stays valid, in seconds. Default `600` (10 minutes).

members.name: otpMaxAge
members.doc:
How long a one-time code stays valid, in seconds — an emailed one and a `phoneOtp()` text
alike. Default `300` (5 minutes).

members.name: otpDigits
members.doc: How many digits a one-time code (email or SMS) has. Default `6`; clamped to `6..10`.

members.name: verifyPath
members.doc:
The same-origin path an email-verification link opens (the link adds `?token=…&email=…`).
Default `{basePath}/verify` — `"/auth/verify"` — the built-in endpoint, which verifies
the address and redirects. Must start with a single `/`.

members.name: resetPath
members.doc:
The same-origin path a password-reset link opens (the link adds `?token=…&email=…`) —
a page YOUR app renders: a form posting `email`, `token` and the new `password` to
`{basePath}/reset/confirm`. Default `{basePath}/reset` — `"/auth/reset"`; the auth
endpoints only claim a POST there, so a GET falls through to e.g.
`app/auth/reset/page.tsx`. Must start with a single `/`.

symbols.name: AuthEvents
symbols.doc: Side-effect hooks on the auth lifecycle. A handler may be async; it is awaited, and a throw is caught and routed to AuthLogger.error — an event handler can never fail a sign-in.
symbols.docFull:
Side-effect hooks on the auth lifecycle. A handler may be async; it is awaited, and a
throw is caught and routed to {@link AuthLogger.error} — an event handler can never
fail a sign-in.

members.name: signIn
members.signature: signIn?: (payload: { user: AuthUser; provider: string; isNewUser?: boolean; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc: A session was issued.

members.name: signOut
members.signature: signOut?: (payload: { session: AuthSession | null; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc: A session was cleared through `/signout`.

members.name: signInFailed
members.signature: signInFailed?: (payload: { provider?: string; reason: SignInFailedReason; providerError?: string; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc: A sign-in attempt was refused (bad credentials, a denied callback, a bad state).

members.name: apiTokenIssued
members.signature: apiTokenIssued?: (payload: { userId: string; tokenId: string; name?: string; scopes?: string[]; expiresAt?: number; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc:
A bearer API token was minted (`issueApiToken`, `POST {basePath}/tokens`). Never carries
the token or its hash.

members.name: apiTokenRevoked
members.signature: apiTokenRevoked?: (payload: { tokenId: string; userId?: string; reason: ApiTokenRevokedReason; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc:
A bearer API token was revoked: by `revokeApiToken` / `DELETE {basePath}/tokens/:id`
(`"revoked"`), by a password reset (`"password_reset"`), or by the first proof of an
unverified account's mailbox (`"email_verified"`) or phone number (`"phone_verified"`) —
the pre-account-hijacking eviction.

members.name: sessionRevoked
members.signature: sessionRevoked?: (payload: { sessionId?: string; userId?: string; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc: A server-side session was revoked (one device, or everywhere).

members.name: createUser
members.signature: createUser?: (payload: { user: AdapterUser; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc: An adapter user record was created.

members.name: linkAccount
members.signature: linkAccount?: (payload: { user: AdapterUser; account: Pick<AdapterAccount, "userId" | "provider" | "providerAccountId" | "type">; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc: A provider account was linked to an existing user.

members.name: verificationRequested
members.signature: verificationRequested?: (payload: { identifier: string; purpose: VerificationPurpose; expiresAt: number; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc:
A verification token was delivered through `sendVerificationRequest` / `hooks.sendEmail` (an
email-verification or password-reset email, or a `magicLink()` / `emailOtp()` sign-in
link or code), or a `phoneOtp()` code through the SMS sender (`purpose: "sms"`, the number as
`identifier`). Fires only for a real send — never for
an unknown address, a throttled request or a failed delivery — and never carries the
token or the link.

members.name: emailVerified
members.signature: emailVerified?: (payload: { user: AdapterUser; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc:
A user proved control of their address: by redeeming an email-verification token, or
by a first magic-link / one-time-code sign-in into an existing unverified account —
whose password, bearer tokens and server-side sessions were retired first
(`sessionRevoked` fired for the sessions).

members.name: phoneVerified
members.signature: phoneVerified?: (payload: { user: AdapterUser; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc:
A user proved control of their phone number by a first `phoneOtp()` sign-in into an
existing account whose number was unverified — whose password, second factors, passkeys,
bearer tokens and server-side sessions were retired first (`sessionRevoked` fired for the
sessions).

members.name: userConverted
members.signature: userConverted?: (payload: { user: AdapterUser; provider: string; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc:
An anonymous user became permanent: a complete anonymous session redeemed an email link /
code or a phone code for an identifier no account had, so the proof was attached to the
anonymous user (same id, `isAnonymous` cleared) instead of creating a new one.

members.name: passwordReset
members.signature: passwordReset?: (payload: { user: AdapterUser; ip?: string }) => Promise<void> | void
members.doc:
A user set a new password by redeeming a password-reset token. Their server-side
sessions have already been revoked when this fires (`sessionRevoked` fired too).

symbols.name: AuthLogger
symbols.doc: Where the framework logs; every method is optional and defaults to silence.
symbols.docFull: Where the framework logs; every method is optional and defaults to silence.

members.name: debug
members.signature: debug?: (message: string, meta?: Record<string, unknown>) => void
members.doc: Verbose flow tracing.

members.name: warn
members.signature: warn?: (message: string, meta?: Record<string, unknown>) => void
members.doc: A recoverable misconfiguration (never a secret).

members.name: error
members.doc: A swallowed failure — a provider round-trip, an adapter write, an event handler.

symbols.name: AuthMfaConfig
symbols.doc: Second-factor (TOTP) policy. Every field is optional; see each default.
symbols.docFull: Second-factor (TOTP) policy. Every field is optional; see each default.

members.name: required
members.doc:
Who must present a second factor: `"enrolled"` (the default) asks only users who have
enrolled one; `"always"` asks everyone, sending a user without a factor to enrol
first. Any other value reads as `"enrolled"`.

members.name: issuer
members.doc:
The issuer label an authenticator app shows next to the account. Default: the host
name of `canonicalOrigin`, else `"denext"`.

members.name: window
members.doc:
How many 30-second TOTP steps of clock drift are accepted either side of now.
Default `1` (±30 seconds); clamped to `0..2`.

members.name: backupCodes
members.doc: How many single-use backup codes enrollment mints. Default `10`; clamped to `0..20`.

members.name: freshness
members.doc:
How recent, in seconds, a second-factor proof must be for an action that demands a
fresh one (step-up). Default `900` (15 minutes); clamped to `0..31536000`. `0` means such
an action always asks for a code.

symbols.name: AuthNativeConfig
symbols.doc: **Native session mode** — sessions for an app whose WebView can't use the __Host- SameSite cookie (a Capacitor shell at capacitor://localhost). The app opens {basePath}/native/authorize in a system browser sheet (openAuthSession), signs in there with any provider, and receives a one-time code at its redirect URI; it exchanges the code plus its PKCE verifier at POST {basePath}/native/token for a short-lived bearer access token and a rotating refresh token. auth(), requireAuth() and requireSession() accept the access token. Needs an adapter with the native session group.
symbols.docFull:
**Native session mode** — sessions for an app whose WebView can't use the `__Host-`
SameSite cookie (a Capacitor shell at `capacitor://localhost`). The app opens
`{basePath}/native/authorize` in a system browser sheet (`openAuthSession`), signs in there
with any provider, and receives a one-time `code` at its redirect URI; it exchanges the
code plus its PKCE verifier at `POST {basePath}/native/token` for a short-lived bearer
access token and a rotating refresh token. `auth()`, `requireAuth()` and `requireSession()`
accept the access token. Needs an adapter with the native session group.

members.name: redirectUris
members.doc:
The app callback URIs a code may be delivered to, matched EXACTLY (e.g.
`"com.example.app://auth/callback"`, or a claimed `https://` universal link). A loopback
`http://127.0.0.1/…` / `http://[::1]/…` entry matches any port (RFC 8252 §7.3), for a
desktop app's ephemeral listener. Plain `http:` elsewhere, `javascript:`, `data:` and
`file:` are refused.

members.name: accessTokenTtl
members.doc: Access-token lifetime in seconds (default 900; clamped to 60..3600).

members.name: refreshTokenTtl
members.doc:
How long a refresh token stays usable, in seconds; each refresh slides it forward (default
30 days; clamped to 1 hour..1 year).

members.name: refreshTokenMaxAge
members.doc:
An absolute cap on a session family, in seconds from its original sign-in: however often
the app refreshes, the family stops refreshing (and is revoked) this long after the user
signed in, and they sign in again. Default: none — a family used within every
`refreshTokenTtl` lives indefinitely. Clamped to 1 hour..10 years.

members.name: refreshReuseInterval
members.doc:
A grace window, in seconds, for two refreshes racing with one refresh token (a background
task and the foreground app, two processes). Within this long after a rotation, presenting
the IMMEDIATELY previous refresh token answers the same token pair that rotation issued,
instead of treating it as a replay and revoking the family. An older generation, or the
previous one after the window, is still a replay. Default `10`, as GoTrue's
`GOTRUE_SECURITY_REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSE_INTERVAL`; `0` is strict (any reuse revokes); clamped
to 0..60. Inside the window a replayed previous token gets the pair its legitimate use
got — set `0` where that matters more than a refresh race.

members.name: codeTtl
members.doc: One-time code lifetime in seconds (default 60; clamped to 10..600).

members.name: requireNonce
members.doc:
Require a server-issued nonce (`POST {basePath}/native/nonce`) in every native id_token
sign-in (default `true`), so a captured id_token can't be replayed.

members.name: apple
members.doc: Native Sign in with Apple (`POST {basePath}/native/apple`).

members.name: google
members.doc: Native Google sign-in (`POST {basePath}/native/google`).

members.name: fetch
members.signature: fetch?: (url: string, init: { method: string; headers: Record<string, string>; body?: string }) => Promise<Response>
members.doc:
Test / advanced seam: the fetch used for the providers' JWKS and Apple's token and revoke
endpoints. Default: `safeFetch`, pinned to the provider's hosts.

symbols.doc: A named author (<meta name="author">, optional <link rel="author">).
symbols.docFull: A named author (`<meta name="author">`, optional `<link rel="author">`).

members.doc: Author name.

members.name: url

symbols.doc: What AuthCallbacks.authorized is asked about.
symbols.docFull: What {@link AuthCallbacks.authorized} is asked about.

members.doc: The live session — already non-null and not MFA-pending when the callback runs.

members.name: request
members.doc: The request being guarded.

symbols.doc: Options for tapChannelAuthorized.
symbols.docFull: Options for {@linkcode tapChannelAuthorized}.

members.doc: A payload the subscriber may receive (decoded; `seq` orders publishes from one instance).

members.name: onEnd
members.doc:
The subscription ended because access ended: a cluster-wide `revoke(key)`, a revoke naming
this subscriber's peer, or a lazy re-authorization that said no. Not called by the disposer.

members.name: peerId
members.doc:
The subscriber's peer id (handed to `authorize` as `ctx.peerId`; a `revoke(key, { peerId })`
naming it ends this subscription). Default: a fresh id per call.

symbols.name: AuthPasskeyAndroidApp
symbols.doc: An Android app in passkeys.androidApps (the shape appLinks.android takes).
symbols.docFull: An Android app in `passkeys.androidApps` (the shape `appLinks.android` takes).

members.name: packageName
members.doc: The application id (`com.example.app`).

members.name: sha256CertFingerprints
members.doc:
The SHA-256 fingerprints of the certificates the app is signed with: `AB:CD:…` (32
colon-separated hex pairs, as `keytool` and the Play Console print them) or 64 hex digits.

symbols.name: AuthPasskeyConfig
symbols.doc: Passkeys (WebAuthn) — sign-in with a platform or roaming authenticator, as a first factor or as the second. Every field is optional; the relying party defaults to canonicalOrigin.
symbols.docFull:
Passkeys (WebAuthn) — sign-in with a platform or roaming authenticator, as a first factor or
as the second. Every field is optional; the relying party defaults to `canonicalOrigin`.

members.name: rpId
members.doc:
The relying party ID credentials are scoped to: the host of `canonicalOrigin` by default,
or a registrable suffix of it (`"example.com"` for `https://app.example.com`) to share
passkeys across subdomains. Every accepted origin's host must equal it or end in
`.<rpId>` (WebAuthn L3 §5.1.4.1).

members.name: rpName
members.doc: The relying party name an authenticator may show. Default: the RP ID.

members.name: origins
members.doc:
The origins a ceremony may come from, matched exactly against `clientDataJSON.origin`.
Default: `[canonicalOrigin]`. Add a second web origin here; an Android app goes in
{@linkcode androidApps} (an `android:apk-key-hash:<43 base64url characters>` entry here is
accepted too, checked for that exact form).

members.name: androidApps
members.doc:
Android apps whose passkey ceremonies are accepted: inside an app, Credential Manager
reports `clientDataJSON.origin` as `android:apk-key-hash:<base64url SHA-256 of the signing
certificate>`, and each listed fingerprint adds that exact origin to {@linkcode origins}.
The app calls `/native/passkey/*` (with `native` sessions configured) or, from a page on
this origin, the cookie rows. Android also requires the domain's `assetlinks.json` to
delegate `get_login_creds` to the app: pass the same objects to `appLinks.android` in
`denext.config.ts`. With Play App Signing, list Play's app signing key (Play Console → Test
and release → App integrity) and the upload / debug keys you test with (`keytool -list -v
-keystore <keystore>`).

members.name: corsOrigins
members.doc:
The web origins allowed to call the passkey endpoints from another origin — a front end
served apart from the auth server (`["https://www.example.com"]` for an auth server at
`https://auth.example.com`). Each must also be in {@linkcode origins} (its page runs the
ceremony). The endpoints then answer their preflights and send credentialed CORS headers to
exactly these origins, and a ceremony started from one completes only from that origin, with
client data naming it — on top of the per-tab ceremony id. Default: none (same-origin only).
Pass `origin` to the `denext/client` passkey calls on that front end.

members.name: userVerification
members.doc:
`"required"` (the default) asks the authenticator to verify the user (biometric, PIN) and
refuses an assertion without the UV flag — such a sign-in is two factors in one, so it
also satisfies a pending second factor. `"preferred"` accepts a presence-only assertion,
which is one factor: a user with TOTP is then still asked for a code.

members.name: timeout
members.doc: How long a ceremony's challenge lives, in seconds. Default `300`; clamped to `30..900`.

members.name: attestation
members.doc:
Attestation policy for new passkeys. Off by default: any supported attestation (`none`,
`packed`, `tpm`, `android-key`, `android-safetynet`, `apple`, `fido-u2f`, `compound`)
registers once its statement verifies, and a certificate in it is not chained to anything
(except `android-safetynet`'s, which must chain to Google's root).

symbols.name: AuthPasskeyMdsConfig
symbols.doc: passkeys.attestation.mds: where the metadata comes from and what it lets through.
symbols.docFull: `passkeys.attestation.mds`: where the metadata comes from and what it lets through.

members.name: url
members.doc:
The BLOB's URL (`https:` only). Default: `https://mds.fidoalliance.org/`. A mirror works:
the BLOB is verified against the pinned FIDO root wherever it came from.

members.name: blob
members.doc:
The BLOB itself (the JWT text), or a function returning it — for a server without
outbound network. Verified exactly like a fetched one; when set, `url` is never fetched.

members.name: revocation
members.doc:
What a revocation status that can't be had (no usable OCSP answer, no usable CRL) means,
for a certificate of the BLOB's or an attestation's path that names an OCSP responder or CRL
distribution points: `"require"` refuses the path (fail closed), `"best-effort"` goes on
without it (a certificate reported revoked is still refused), `"off"` asks nothing.
Default: `passkeys.attestation.revocation` (`"hard"` is `"require"`, `"soft"` is
`"best-effort"`); with neither, `"require"`, or `"best-effort"` when {@linkcode blob}
supplies the BLOB.

members.name: timeoutMs
members.doc: The fetch timeout, ms. Default `15000`.

members.name: maxBytes
members.doc: The largest BLOB accepted, bytes. Default 32 MiB.

members.name: allowUnattested
members.doc:
Accept `none` and self attestation (no certificate, so no model is proven), still refusing
an AAGUID whose metadata reports compromise. Default `false`: only an attestation that
chains to its authenticator's metadata roots registers. Synced passkeys attest `none`, so
turn this on unless every user has a certified security key.

members.name: allowUnknownAuthenticators
members.doc:
Accept a certificate attestation whose AAGUID has no metadata entry (its chain is then not
checked). Default `false`.

symbols.name: AuthPasskeyRevocationPolicy
symbols.doc: passkeys.attestation.revocation: "soft" goes on when no OCSP answer or CRL can be had, "hard" refuses.
symbols.docFull:
`passkeys.attestation.revocation`: `"soft"` goes on when no OCSP answer or CRL can be had,
`"hard"` refuses.

symbols.name: AuthProvider
symbols.signature: type AuthProvider = OAuthProvider | CredentialsProvider | EmailProvider | PhoneProvider | SamlProvider
symbols.doc: Any configured provider.
symbols.docFull: Any configured provider.

symbols.name: AuthSession
symbols.doc: The signed (readable, tamper-evident) session payload. Never stores tokens/secrets.
symbols.docFull: The signed (readable, tamper-evident) session payload. Never stores tokens/secrets.

members.name: user
members.doc: The signed-in user.

members.name: provider
members.doc: The provider id that authenticated this session.

members.name: expiresAt
members.doc: Expiry, epoch seconds.

members.name: sessionId
members.doc:
The server-side session id — present only when `denextAuth` runs with a
`sessionStore`. Pass it to `revokeSession` to end this one session (e.g. "sign out
this device"); stateless sessions have no id.

members.name: sid
members.doc:
A stateless cookie session's own random id (128 bits, base64url), minted with the session
and sealed in its httpOnly cookie; `/auth/session` and the client hooks leave it out.
SAML Single Logout names a session by it: an IdP's LogoutRequest puts exactly the sessions it
names on the auth adapter's revocation list, and a revoked session reads as signed out. A
cookie issued before denext minted it has none and can't be targeted. `revokeSession(sid)`
ends the session through the same list, and `currentSessionId()` reads it on the server.
(A store-backed session's id is {@linkcode sessionId}.)

members.name: nativeSessionId
members.doc:
The native-app session family this request authenticated with — present only when the
caller presented a native access token (`Authorization: Bearer nat_…`, see
{@link AuthNativeConfig}). Such a session is never slid forward and sets no cookie.

members.name: v
members.doc:
Payload version. Absent (or `1`) on a session issued before 2.5; `2` on every session
denext issues now. The cookie's MAC domain is unchanged, so a v1 cookie keeps
verifying — readers just treat the fields below as absent.

members.name: issuedAt
members.doc:
When this session payload was last issued, epoch seconds: at sign-in, and again each
time sliding expiry (`session.updateAge`) re-issues the session — a slide re-stamps
`issuedAt` along with `expiresAt`. With sliding on it is therefore the time of the
last slide, not of the sign-in, so an age measured from it (the `mfa.freshness` rule)
says nothing about when a factor was proven (that is `authTime`). Absent on a v1
payload, where readers infer `expiresAt - maxAge`.

members.name: authTime
members.doc:
When the user last authenticated, epoch seconds: set at sign-in and again at a
second-factor step-up, and never moved by sliding expiry. It, not `issuedAt`, says how
recently a factor was proven: the `mfa.freshness` rule for `/mfa/disable`, and the recent
sign-in `/mfa/enroll` asks for. Absent on a session issued before 2.5.0-rc.3.

members.name: authTimeMs
members.doc:
{@link authTime} in epoch milliseconds: what "sign out everywhere" (`sessionsValidAfter`)
compares, so a sign-in in the same second as a revocation is told apart from one before it.
Absent on a session issued before 4.6.0, which counts as signed in at the start of its
`authTime` second.

members.name: mfaPending
members.doc:
Set while the user has passed the first factor but not yet the second. A pending
session **fails closed**: `auth()` reports `null` for it, so every guard built on
`auth()` (requireAuth, requireSession, Live `authorize`, Server Actions) refuses too.
Only the MFA endpoints read a pending session. Absent means the session is complete.

members.name: amr
members.doc:
RFC 8176 authentication-method references — how the user proved identity
(e.g. `["pwd"]`, `["pwd", "otp"]`). Absent on a v1 payload; readers treat that as `[]`.

members.name: saml
members.doc:
For a session a `saml()` provider's sign-in started: the assertion's NameID (with its Format
and the AuthnStatement's SessionIndex, when given) — what SAML Single Logout names the
session by. Set by the framework; a `callbacks.session` result can't change it.

symbols.name: AuthSessionConfig
symbols.doc: Session lifetime + storage strategy.
symbols.docFull: Session lifetime + storage strategy.

members.name: strategy
members.doc:
`"cookie"` (default) keeps the whole payload in the signed cookie — stateless,
multi-replica-safe, only expiry ends it. `"database"` stores the payload server-side
and puts only a random id in the cookie, so sessions are revocable; it requires a
store — either {@link AuthConfig.sessionStore} or an adapter that exposes
`sessions` — and throws at config time when neither is present.

members.name: maxAge
members.doc: Session lifetime in seconds (default 7 days). Overrides the legacy top-level `maxAge`.

members.name: updateAge
members.doc:
Refresh a session's expiry when it is older than this many seconds — "sliding"
sessions. `0` (the default) never refreshes. Only endpoints that own the `Response`
can set a cookie, so the refresh happens on `GET {basePath}/session`, `requireAuth`,
`requireSession` and `updateAuthSession()` — never inside a bare `auth()`.

members.name: maxLifetime
members.doc:
The absolute session lifetime in seconds: a hard ceiling counted from the sign-in
(`authTime`) that sliding refresh never extends. A session is refused once it is this
old, whatever its `expiresAt` says, on both strategies; a step-up to a second factor is a
new authentication and starts a new ceiling. Default: 30 days, or `maxAge` when that is
longer, so a session that never slides is unaffected. Must be a whole number of seconds
no shorter than `maxAge` (`denextAuth()` throws otherwise). Native app sessions have their
own cap, `native.refreshTokenMaxAge`.

symbols.name: AuthSessionSaml
symbols.doc: The SAML subject of a session a saml() provider started (AuthSession.saml).
symbols.docFull: The SAML subject of a session a `saml()` provider started ({@linkcode AuthSession.saml}).

members.name: nameId
members.doc: The Subject's NameID.

members.name: nameIdFormat
members.doc: The NameID's Format, when the assertion gave one.

members.name: sessionIndex
members.doc: The AuthnStatement's SessionIndex, when the assertion gave one.

symbols.name: AuthUser
symbols.doc: A normalized user profile — the non-sensitive identity denext stores in the session.
symbols.docFull: A normalized user profile — the non-sensitive identity denext stores in the session.

members.name: id
members.doc: Stable provider-scoped user id.

members.name: name
members.doc: Display name, if the provider supplies one.

members.name: email
members.doc:
Email, if granted. Dropped by the built-in OIDC mappers when the provider marks
it `email_verified: false` — so an app that links accounts by email can't be fed
an attacker-chosen, unverified address. Check {@link emailVerified} before trusting
it for account linking.

members.name: emailVerified
members.doc:
Whether the provider asserted the email is verified (`email_verified` claim).
`undefined` when the provider doesn't say. Never treat an unverified/absent value
as proof of ownership when linking to an existing local account.

members.name: image
members.doc: Avatar URL, if any.

members.name: roles
members.doc:
Authorization roles carried in the session — what `requireAuth(request, { role })` and
`requireSession({ role })` match (any-of). Populate them in `callbacks.signIn` /
`callbacks.session`, or from an {@link ./adapter.ts | AuthAdapter} user record. Absent
means "no roles", so a role check on a session without them always refuses.

members.name: isAnonymous
members.doc:
`true` for an anonymous user (`POST {basePath}/anonymous`, `signInAnonymously()`): signed
in with no email or phone yet. It becomes permanent — and loses the flag — by redeeming an
email link / code or a phone code for an identifier no other account has. Absent otherwise.

symbols.name: AwaitableCookieStore
symbols.doc: cookies()'s return: usable synchronously AND awaitable (await cookies(), Next 15).
symbols.docFull: `cookies()`'s return: usable synchronously AND awaitable (`await cookies()`, Next 15).

symbols.name: AwaitableDraftMode
symbols.doc: draftMode()'s return: usable synchronously AND awaitable (await draftMode(), Next 15).
symbols.docFull: `draftMode()`'s return: usable synchronously AND awaitable (`await draftMode()`, Next 15).

symbols.name: AwaitableHeaders

symbols.name: BackoffOptions
symbols.doc: How long to wait before restart number n: initialMs, then factor times that per restart, capped at maxMs, with up to jitter of it taken off at random so restarts that failed together do not retry together.
symbols.docFull:
How long to wait before restart number `n`: `initialMs`, then `factor` times that per restart,
capped at `maxMs`, with up to `jitter` of it taken off at random so restarts that failed
together do not retry together.

members.name: initialMs
members.doc: The first restart's delay in ms.

members.name: maxMs
members.doc: The longest delay in ms (at most 2^31-1, a timer's limit).

members.name: factor
members.doc: The growth per restart (default 2; `1` is a fixed delay).

members.name: jitter
members.doc:
The share of each delay taken off at random, `0` to `1` (default `0.2`: a delay lands
between 80% and 100% of the exponential value). `0` makes the delays exact.

symbols.name: backupCodeMatcher
symbols.signature: backupCodeMatcher(hasher: Hasher, code: string): (hash: string) => Promise<boolean>
symbols.doc: Build the matches predicate the adapter's consumeBackupCode walks the stored hashes with. The presented code is normalised (spaces and hyphens stripped, lowercased); a malformed one yields a predicate that matches nothing — yet still runs one hasher.verify per stored hash, so a garbage submission costs what a wrong code does.

symbols.name: buildAuthnRequest
symbols.signature: buildAuthnRequest(options: BuildAuthnRequestOptions): Promise<{ id: string; url: string }>
symbols.doc: Build an AuthnRequest and the IdP URL that carries it (HTTP-Redirect binding: the XML is DEFLATE-compressed, base64-encoded and URL-encoded into SAMLRequest). The request names this SP's HTTP-POST ACS URL, and is signed (SigAlg + Signature) when sp.signingKey is set. Remember the returned id (with the RelayState) and pass it as expectedInResponseTo when the Response arrives.
symbols.docFull:

DEFLATE-compressed, base64-encoded and URL-encoded into `SAMLRequest`). The request names

symbols.name: CacheStore
symbols.doc: The pluggable backend behind denext's data cache and page (ISR) cache.
symbols.docFull:
The pluggable backend behind denext's data cache and page (ISR) cache.

The default is the durable `node:sqlite` store (resolved by
{@linkcode resolveDefaultCacheStore}, with an in-memory fallback). Inject a store
backed by a shared cache (Redis, etc.) with {@linkcode setCacheStore} so cached data
and rendered pages are shared across replicas and invalidation reaches every instance.

Methods may return synchronously or as a Promise; denext always awaits them.
`get*` must return only **fresh** entries — an implementation is responsible
for treating an expired `expiresAt` as a miss (and may evict it).

members.doc: Store a cached page under `key`.

members.doc: Purge every data entry and page carrying `tag`.
