symbols.name: DraftTokenStore
symbols.doc: Backing store for server-minted draft tokens. Draft mode is "on" only when the request cookie holds a token this server issued via enable(); a forged or guessed value is not in the store, so it cannot turn draft mode on.
symbols.docFull:
Backing store for server-minted draft tokens. Draft mode is "on" only when the
request cookie holds a token this server issued via `enable()`; a forged or
guessed value is not in the store, so it cannot turn draft mode on.

The default store is in-memory (per-process, resets on restart). A
multi-instance deployment can inject a store backed by a shared cache
(Redis/KV) via {@linkcode setDraftTokenStore} so a token minted on one
instance is honored on another. The store is synchronous to keep
{@linkcode draftMode}'s `isEnabled` synchronous; back an async store with a
synchronously-readable cache, or mint signed/stateless tokens instead.

symbols.name: enrollTotp
symbols.doc: Start a TOTP enrollment: mint a secret, store it as an **unverified** TOTP factor, and return it with the provisioning URI (issuer mfa.issuer, account user.email ?? user.id). Earlier unverified TOTP factors are replaced. While a verified TOTP factor exists another one is added only from a session that proved a second factor recently (hasFreshFactor), and a pending session adds none while any verified factor exists; otherwise the answer is already_enrolled — a first factor alone must never add a factor next to one.
symbols.docFull:
Start a TOTP enrollment: mint a secret, store it as an **unverified** TOTP factor, and return
it with the provisioning URI (issuer `mfa.issuer`, account `user.email ?? user.id`). Earlier
unverified TOTP factors are replaced. While a verified TOTP factor exists another one is
added only from a session that proved a second factor recently (`hasFreshFactor`), and a
pending session adds none while any verified factor exists; otherwise the answer is
`already_enrolled` — a first factor alone must never add a factor next to one.

From a complete session this needs a recent sign-in (`session.authTime` within
`mfa.freshness`, five minutes at least), exactly as `POST {basePath}/mfa/enroll` does: a
stolen long-lived session must not set up a factor of its own and lock the owner out. A
pending session (`mfa.required: "always"`) is minutes old and may enroll.

params.name: session
params.doc: The enrolling user's session (auth(), or pendingMfaSession()).

symbols.returns: { ok: true, factorId, secret, uri }, or { ok: false, error }.

symbols.name: EnrollTotpResult
symbols.signature: type EnrollTotpResult = ({ ok: true } & TotpEnrollment) | { ok: false; error: "already_enrolled" | "reauth_required" }
symbols.doc: The outcome of enrollTotp: the fresh secret and its URI, or why none was minted — "already_enrolled" (a verified TOTP factor exists and this session did not just prove a second factor) or "reauth_required" (a complete session that didn't sign in recently).
symbols.docFull:
The outcome of {@linkcode enrollTotp}: the fresh secret and its URI, or why none was minted
— `"already_enrolled"` (a verified TOTP factor exists and this session did not just prove a
second factor) or `"reauth_required"` (a complete session that didn't sign in recently).

The object form may also list the response headers the error carries (name → description, e.g. { "retry-after": "Seconds until the window resets" }) — documentation only, which @denext/openapi renders on that status's response; set the header itself with fail(code, { headers }).

symbols.name: ExperimentalConfig
symbols.doc: Next.js's experimental block, as a migrated next.config carries it into denext.config.ts. Each member is Next.js's own spelling of a top-level DenextConfig field, kept as an obsolete alias for migrated Next apps: honored (with a dev warning) when the top-level field is absent, and ignored when both are set. Next 16's experimental.cacheComponents is honored the same way (see resolveCacheComponents) but is not a typed member. denext's own former experimental.* keys (compiler, asyncContext, features, nodeResolve) were removed in 3.0; the config validator rejects them.
symbols.docFull:
Next.js's `experimental` block, as a migrated `next.config` carries it into
`denext.config.ts`. Each member is Next.js's own spelling of a top-level
{@link DenextConfig} field, kept as an obsolete alias for migrated Next apps: honored
(with a dev warning) when the top-level field is absent, and ignored when both are set.
Next 16's `experimental.cacheComponents` is honored the same way (see
{@linkcode resolveCacheComponents}) but is not a typed member. denext's own former
`experimental.*` keys (`compiler`, `asyncContext`, `features`, `nodeResolve`) were removed
in 3.0; the config validator rejects them.

members.doc:
Link a first SSO sign-in to an EXISTING account with the same email address (a password,
magic-link or OAuth user) when the address is on one of this provider's {@linkcode domains}.
Default `false`, as in GoTrue: such a sign-in is refused (`email_exists`) rather than handed

- `"always"` — **every** locale is prefixed, including the default (`/en/about`);

request thousands of arbitrary widths, each forcing a fresh WASM decode/resize.

endpoint refuses any other quality (400), bounding the distinct-encode surface

Next.js `images.maximumRedirects`). Defaults to `3`; `0` disables redirects.

**Dangerous.** Allow remote sources that resolve to loopback/private/link-local
addresses, disabling the SSRF address guard for the image optimizer (Next.js 16

symbols.docFull:
Build a per-process, in-memory {@link ./adapter.ts | AuthAdapter}: every method group
(users, accounts, verification tokens, credentials, API tokens, MFA, native app sessions,
passkeys, account deletion) plus a
`sessions` store and `close()`. Ids are `crypto.randomUUID()` unless the caller
supplies one; emails are matched case-insensitively and whitespace-trimmed.

Nothing persists across a restart and nothing is shared between replicas — use it for
development, tests and single-process demos, and
{@link ./sqlite-adapter.ts | sqliteAuthAdapter} for anything real.
symbols.returns: The adapter, ready to pass as denextAuth({ adapter }).

symbols.name: JobHistoryStore
symbols.doc: Where job run history is kept — the seam behind jobs: { history }.
symbols.docFull:
Where job run history is kept — the seam behind `jobs: { history }`.

denext records one row per completed run: its start (`startedAt`), how it ended (`ok`: it
finished; `!ok`: it threw, with the error's head in `detail`) and, for a job with `retry`,
the attempt. The default store is a SQLite file in `.denext/` ({@linkcode
sqliteJobHistoryStore}); {@linkcode postgresJobHistoryStore} keeps it in Postgres, shared by
every replica. Any object with these methods works:

```ts
// denext.config.ts
import { postgresJobHistoryStore } from "denext/server";
export default {
  jobs: { history: { store: postgresJobHistoryStore({ url: Deno.env.get("DATABASE_URL") }) } },
};
```

The contract a store must keep: **recording never fails or delays a run.** `record` is
called on the tail of every run and never awaited; it must not throw (a returned promise must
not reject), and a store that cannot write drops the row. The readers never throw either:
an unreadable store is `{ available: false, reason }`.

members.name: record
members.doc:
Record one completed run. Called on the run's tail, never awaited: must not throw, and a
returned promise must not reject.

members.name: read
members.doc:
The panel summary: per-job standing inside the window, and the recent feed (newest first).
Reads only: no table is created or migrated to answer (nothing recorded yet is
`{ available: false, reason }`).

members.name: history
members.doc:
Record every job run — scheduled and on demand — to `.denext/jobs.db`, so `denext ui`'s
Cron panel can show last status, success/failure counts and a recent-run feed.

Off unless set: denext writes no run history unasked. Once on, recording can never fail or
delay a run — a read-only filesystem or a locked file degrades to no history instead.

Each row keeps the run's output in plain text: the tail of a string the handler returned
(up to 2 KB) and, for a failure, the error's message and stack. A task that returns a token,
a DSN or another secret should return nothing instead. The file is `jobs.db` (with its
`-wal`/`-shm` siblings) inside the build output directory, `.denext/` by default, created
owner-only (mode 0600) where the platform has file modes.

The object form picks where the history is kept: `{ store }` takes any
{@link JobHistoryStore} — `postgresJobHistoryStore({ url })` shares one history across
every replica — and `{ maxRuns }` sets the default store's cap. `{}` is the same as `true`.

```ts
jobs: { history: { store: postgresJobHistoryStore({ url: Deno.env.get("DATABASE_URL") }) } }
```

members.name: historyMaxRuns
members.doc:
Runs kept per job before the oldest are dropped (default 500).

Per job rather than overall, so a job running every minute cannot evict a daily job's
history. A job running more often than roughly every 20 minutes fills this inside a week,
so raise it for such a job if its counts should cover the whole window.

symbols.name: LiveConfig
symbols.doc: Live Server Components security policy (the top-level live config). Presence rooms and useLive data subscriptions are **default-deny**, identically in dev and production: without a policy hook (or LiveConfig.allowAnonymous) the hub refuses joins/subscriptions — so a persistent socket can't read other users' presence or run registered actions — and surfaces a loud, actionable error the first time it runs (there is no dev/prod divergence that could let it work locally and silently break in production). Resource caps in LiveLimits always apply.
symbols.docFull:
Live Server Components security policy (the top-level `live` config). Presence rooms and
`useLive` data subscriptions are **default-deny**, identically in dev and
production: without a policy hook (or {@link LiveConfig.allowAnonymous}) the hub
refuses joins/subscriptions — so a persistent socket can't read other users'
presence or run registered actions — and surfaces a loud, actionable error the
first time it runs (there is no dev/prod divergence that could let it work locally
and silently break in production). Resource caps in {@link LiveLimits} always apply.

members.name: allowAnonymous
members.doc:
Permit presence-room joins with no policy hook — opens rooms to any same-origin
client. It does **not** open arbitrary data: `useLive` data subscriptions still
require the per-action `liveReadable(...)` opt-in (or a `canSubscribe` hook), so
enabling anonymous presence never exposes unmarked/mutating actions on the socket.
Only set it for genuinely public collaboration. Defaults to `false` (deny in dev
and production alike).

symbols.name: LiveLimits
symbols.doc: Resource limits for the Live WebSocket hub. Each has a safe built-in default.
symbols.docFull: Resource limits for the Live WebSocket hub. Each has a safe built-in default.

members.name: maxConnections
members.doc: Max simultaneous connections (default 10000).

members.name: maxConnectionsPerIp
members.doc:
Max simultaneous connections from one client address (default 64) — the address
`clientIp()` answers in the upgrade request. An IPv6 address counts as its /64. A handshake
past it is refused with 429. A connection whose address is a loopback, private, link-local or
unique-local socket peer is not capped per address (only by `maxConnections`) unless
`trustForwardedHeaders` is set: behind a reverse proxy every visitor shares the proxy's
address, so set `trustForwardedHeaders` (or `DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1`) there to cap each
visitor's own address; the server warns once when it skips the cap.

members.name: maxSubscriptionsPerConnection
members.doc: Max `useLive` subscriptions per connection (default 64).

members.name: maxRoomsPerConnection
members.doc: Max presence rooms per connection (default 32).

members.name: maxPeersPerRoom
members.doc:
Max peers in one presence room (default 1000). A room's membership is otherwise bounded
only by `maxConnections`, and `broadcastRoom` re-encodes O(N) bytes to N peers on every
join/update/leave, so an unbounded room is O(N²) fan-out fleet-wide — a join past the cap
is refused with `limit`.

members.name: maxBoundaries
members.doc: Max `<Live>` boundaries watched per connection (default 256).

members.name: maxMessageBytes
members.doc: Max inbound message size in bytes (default 65536).

members.name: maxSubscriptionInputBytes
members.doc:
Max size in bytes of one subscription's input / args (default 16384): the input is
stored for the connection's lifetime and re-used on every recompute, so it is capped
tighter than a frame.

members.name: maxChannelsPerConnection
members.doc: Max `useChannel` subscriptions per connection (default 32).

members.name: maxChannelPayloadBytes
members.doc: Max bytes of one channel payload (default 16384); `publish` throws past it.

members.name: channelAuthTtlSeconds
idleTimeoutSeconds
members.doc: Socket idle timeout in seconds passed to `Deno.upgradeWebSocket` (default 120).

members.name: maxConcurrentRenders
members.doc:
Fleet-wide cap on concurrent live re-renders/recomputes (default 40). A single
`revalidateTag` can match every connected socket; this bounds how many full-route
re-renders (`<Live>`) and `useLive` fetcher runs execute at once so one
invalidation can't spawn one render per connection simultaneously (a self-inflicted
DoS amplification). Excess work queues and drains as slots free.

members.name: renderTimeoutSeconds
members.doc:
Per-render deadline in seconds (default 30). A `<Live>` re-render or `useLive`
fetcher run holds one of the `maxConcurrentRenders` slots for its whole duration;
without a deadline a hung user fetcher pins its slot forever, and enough hung
fetchers peg the concurrency gate and stall the whole live fleet. On timeout the
run is aborted (a cooperative `AbortSignal` reaches the fetcher's `fetch`/cache
reads) and its slot released; the client gets an error/refresh frame. On by default
— there is no "disable" value (an invalid one falls back to 30s). It also bounds how long
one live-view mount (`defineLiveView`, `defineLustreView`) may hold its connection's mount
queue; past it the mount is answered `failed` and the next one runs.

members.name: maxViewsPerConnection
members.doc:
Max live views (`defineLiveView`) one connection may hold mounted (default 16). It also caps
the connection's mount queue: at most `max(4, 2 × maxViewsPerConnection)` mounts waiting or
running at once; a mount past that is refused with `limit` and never queued.

members.name: maxViewBytesPerConnection
members.doc:
Max bytes of server-held state per connection across its live views (default 1048576): each
view's model (as JSON) plus its last rendered tree. An update or render past it ends that view
with a `limit` error.

members.name: viewResumeSeconds
members.doc:
Seconds a dropped connection's live views stay on the server for the client to resume after
a reconnect (default 30). Past it, or on another instance, the next mount runs `init` again.

members.name: maxParkedViews
members.doc: Max live views waiting to be resumed across the server (default 1000; the oldest go first).

members.name: viewTokenMaxAgeSeconds
members.doc:
Seconds a live view's signed props token (rendered into the page) is accepted for a mount or
a resume (default 86400, a day). An older one is refused as `gone`, and the browser re-renders
the route once for a fresh token. A page cached longer than this (`force-static`, or ISR with a
longer `revalidate`) needs a larger value.

symbols.docFull:
Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) — OIDC v2.0 endpoints, `id_token` verified
against the tenant's JWKS. A single tenant, or the multi-tenant aliases (`common`,
`organizations`, `consumers`; see {@link MicrosoftEntraOptions.tenant}). Claims come from
the verified `id_token`, so no Microsoft Graph call is made.

members.name: tenant
members.doc:
The directory (tenant): a tenant id (GUID) or a verified domain such as `"contoso.com"` for
a single-tenant app, or one of the multi-tenant aliases:

- `"organizations"` — any work or school tenant (personal Microsoft accounts are refused);
- `"common"` — any work or school tenant AND personal Microsoft accounts;
- `"consumers"` — personal Microsoft accounts only.

For `common` / `organizations` the `id_token`'s issuer is checked against its own `tid`
claim (`https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tid}/v2.0`, the template issuer Microsoft's
discovery document declares), with the signature checked against the common key set. Any
tenant can then sign in, so list the ones you serve in {@linkcode allowedTenants}.

With any alias the account is keyed on `tid` + `oid`, and the `email` claim is used only
when the optional claim `xms_edov` is `true` (add it to the app registration); otherwise the
account has no email, so another tenant can't claim an address through it.

members.name: allowedTenants
members.doc:
With `tenant: "common"` or `"organizations"`: the tenant ids (GUIDs) allowed to sign in.
Recommended — without it, a user of ANY Entra tenant (including one an attacker creates)
can sign in. Not accepted with a single tenant or `consumers`.

cookie check (CSRF) exempts exactly the requests `auth()` authenticates by the token, never
one whose session comes from the cookie.

members.doc: URL-safe provider id (the `[provider]` route segment), e.g. `"google"`.

members.doc: `"oidc"` verifies an `id_token`; `"oauth"` calls a userinfo endpoint.

members.doc: Authorization endpoint.

members.doc: Token endpoint.

members.name: userinfoUrl
members.doc: Userinfo endpoint (OAuth providers, or OIDC when you prefer userinfo).

members.name: userEmailsUrl
members.doc:
Optional endpoint returning the account's email list (e.g. GitHub
`/user/emails`), fetched with the access token after userinfo. Its result is
passed to {@link profile} as `emails`, so the mapper can pick a *verified* address
rather than trusting an unverified `userinfo.email`.

members.name: issuer
members.doc: Expected `iss` for id_token verification (OIDC).

members.name: jwksUrl
members.doc: JWKS URL for id_token signature keys (OIDC).

members.name: scopes
members.doc: Requested scopes.

members.name: clientId
members.doc: OAuth client id.

members.name: clientSecret
members.doc: OAuth client secret.

members.name: profile
members.doc: Map the token/userinfo/claims result to a normalized {@link AuthUser}.

members.name: authorizationParams
members.doc: Extra authorization-request query params (e.g. `{ access_type: "offline" }`).

members.name: tokenEndpointAuthMethod
members.doc:
How the client authenticates at the token endpoint (RFC 6749 §2.3.1).
`"client_secret_post"` (the default) sends `client_id` / `client_secret` in the form body;
`"client_secret_basic"` sends them as an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header instead, which
some providers (X, Zoom, Notion) require.

members.name: responseMode
members.doc:
How the provider returns the authorization response (OAuth 2.0 Multiple Response Type
Encoding Practices §2.1). `"query"` (the default) redirects back with `?code=…&state=…`,
answered by `GET {basePath}/callback/:id`. `"form_post"` (OAuth 2.0 Form Post Response
Mode §2) has the browser POST them as a form to the same URL, which Sign in with Apple
requires to hand over a user's name and email. A form_post flow's transaction cookie is
`SameSite=None; Secure` — the provider's cross-site POST must carry it — and its callback
accepts only the POST: a GET carrying a code is refused.

members.name: checks
members.doc:
The protections the flow runs besides `state`, as Auth.js's provider `checks` name them.
Unset (the default): PKCE (S256), plus a `nonce` for an `"oidc"` provider. Set: PKCE only
when the list has `"pkce"`, and a `nonce` only for an `"oidc"` provider whose list has
`"nonce"` — for a provider that refuses a `code_verifier` it didn't ask for (`["state"]`).
`state` is sent and verified on every flow whatever the list says: `"state"` and `"none"`
change nothing about it.

members.name: tokenRequestParams
members.doc:
Extra form parameters on the token request (TikTok's `client_key`). They never replace one
the flow sets itself (`grant_type`, `code`, `redirect_uri`, `code_verifier`, the client
credentials).

members.name: userinfoRequest
members.doc:
Read the profile with a request of the provider's own shape instead of a `GET` of
`userinfoUrl` with the access token as a Bearer header (a `POST`, API-key headers, an id
from the token response in the URL). `fetch` is the provider fetch, pinned to its hosts.

members.name: idTokenAlg
members.doc:
`"HS256"`: the provider signs its `id_token` with HMAC-SHA256 under the client secret, as
its specification requires (LINE). It is verified with the secret, and no other algorithm is
accepted. Unset: the issuer's JWKS (RS / PS / ES algorithms).

members.name: allowedHosts
members.doc:
Hosts `safeFetch` may reach for this provider (token/userinfo/jwks). Derived
from the configured endpoints when omitted. A `*.domain` entry admits that domain's
subdomains (not the apex), for an endpoint discovery finds on a per-tenant subdomain.

members.name: discovery
members.doc:
Fill the endpoints from the provider's OIDC discovery document
(`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`) instead of hard-coding them. The
fetched document must declare exactly this `issuer` or it is refused, and the
request is pinned to the issuer's host.

members.name: strictAudience
members.doc:
Refuse an `id_token` whose `aud` lists audiences besides this client unless it also
carries an `azp` naming this client (RFC 7519 §4.1.3 / OIDC Core §3.1.3.7 step 4).
Defaults to **on**; set `false` only for a provider that legitimately mints
multi-audience tokens without `azp`.

members.name: tenantIssuer
members.doc:
A multi-tenant issuer (`microsoftEntra({ tenant: "common" | "organizations" })`): `issuer`
is a template carrying `{tenantid}`, and an `id_token` is accepted only when its `iss` is
exactly that template with the token's own tenant claim (`claim`, a GUID) substituted —
the templated issuer the provider's discovery document declares. `allowedTenants` limits
which tenants may sign in; `excludedTenants` refuses some (`organizations` excludes the
personal-account tenant).

members.name: allowDangerousEmailAccountLinking
members.doc:
DANGEROUS: when this provider returns an email that already belongs to a local
account, link to it even though that account's address is **unverified**. Off by
default, and off is the safe answer — an attacker who registers an unverified local
account with a victim's address would otherwise take it over at the victim's first
provider login.

symbols.name: oidc
symbols.doc: A generic OIDC provider (Authorization Code + PKCE, id_token verified via JWKS).
symbols.docFull:
A generic OIDC provider (Authorization Code + PKCE, `id_token` verified via JWKS).

Two forms:
```ts
oidc({ issuer: "https://idp.example.com", clientId, clientSecret }); // discovery
oidc({ issuer, authorizationUrl, tokenUrl, jwksUrl, clientId, clientSecret }); // explicit
```
The issuer-only form resolves the endpoints from
`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` and refuses a document that declares a
different `issuer`. Passing *some* of the three endpoints is a configuration error: it
would silently mix a hand-written endpoint with a discovered one.

params.doc: Issuer (+ optional endpoints/mapper) and the app's client credentials.

`{ ios: "out-ios", android: "out-android" }` (each from `denext export --platform <target>`).
A request is served the export its `x-denext-ota-platform` header names — `checkForUiUpdate`
and the desktop updater send their target on the manifest request and every download — and
one without the header the `web` export, if given. A target with no export is not served.

members.name: channels
members.doc:
Serve per-channel releases with staged rollouts instead of one `dir`: the path of a channels
file (`ota-channels.json`, re-read when its mtime changes, release paths relative to it;
`denext ota channel` / `denext ota promote` write it), or the {@linkcode OtaChannelsFile}
itself (release paths relative to the working directory).

A request follows the channel its `x-denext-ota-channel` header names (absent: the file's
`default`; an unknown or malformed name is not served — it never falls back to another
channel). A channel's `rollout` candidate goes to the share of devices whose
`x-denext-ota-install-id` falls in the rollout bucket (`otaRolloutBucket`); a request without
a valid install id always gets the stable `release`. The manifest and every file of one
request come from the same release, and each release's manifest is served unchanged, so its
signature is verified on the device exactly as with `dir`. The client sends both headers
with `checkForUiUpdate({ channel })` (denext/mobile), on the manifest request and on every
native file download.

members.name: basePath
members.doc:
The URL path the UI is served under, e.g. `"/mobile-ui"` (the client's `baseUrl` is
then `https://host/mobile-ui`). Default `""`: the origin root.

members.name: cors
members.doc:
Answer CORS for the web app's manifest request (`checkForUiUpdate` / `prepareUiUpdate`
fetch `_denext/ota.json` from the webview's origin, and an `Authorization` header makes that
a preflighted request). `true` allows the Capacitor webview origins `capacitor://localhost`
(iOS), `https://localhost` and `http://localhost` (Android); a string or list allows exactly
those origins. An allowed `OPTIONS` preflight is answered `204` with
`Access-Control-Allow-Headers: authorization`, and `GET`/`HEAD` responses carry
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` for an allowed `Origin`. Default: no CORS headers, and
`OPTIONS` is not answered. A preflight carries no credentials, so route `OPTIONS` to the
handler before your auth check. Native file downloads are not subject to CORS.

symbols.name: otaRolloutBucket
symbols.signature: otaRolloutBucket(channel: string, candidateVersion: string, installId: string): Promise<number>
symbols.doc:
The stable rollout bucket of one install for one candidate release: the first four bytes of SHA-256(denext-ota-rollout
<channel>
<candidateVersion>
<installId>) as a big-endian uint32, modulo 10 000. A device is in a rollout of percent when the bucket is below percent * 100. Salting with the candidate's manifest version draws a fresh cohort for each release, while raising the percentage for the same candidate only ever adds devices.
symbols.docFull:
The stable rollout bucket of one install for one candidate release: the first four bytes of
SHA-256(`denext-ota-rollout\n<channel>\n<candidateVersion>\n<installId>`) as a big-endian
uint32, modulo 10 000. A device is in a rollout of `percent` when the bucket is below
`percent * 100`. Salting with the candidate's manifest version draws a fresh cohort for each
release, while raising the percentage for the same candidate only ever adds devices.

The rendered-page store for Incremental Static Regeneration. A thin façade

transparently (replicas of one build share its build id).

Omitted, entries are keyed by path alone.

be read through {@linkcode headers} / {@linkcode cookies} from `denext/server`,

form (or, under `mfa.required: "always"` for a user with no factor yet, the enrollment

out, and it is never slid forward. It is short-lived, and the step-up replaces it with
a fresh session rather than upgrading it. One whose user has since been banned or deleted,

publishes itself: `index.html`, denext's own output under `_denext/` (`client/`, `pages/`,
`fonts/`, `ota.json`, `platform.txt`, `desktop-preload.js`), the `spa.assetsDir` directory and,
in an export, any file the build already wrote there (a rendered page, a client chunk).
An asset given by `name` instead of `fileName` gets a content-hashed name
({@linkcode EmittedHashedAsset}), which may sit in the `spa.assetsDir` directory. Resolves to
the file name it was published under.

members.doc:
Contribute a prepare step that generates inputs the app imports — run at `denext build` AND at
`denext dev` startup, plus on every change under its `watch` globs during dev (so generated types
and data stay live as you edit). Use this (not {@linkcode addBuildStep}) for codegen.

members.name: addCommand
members.doc:
Contribute a first-class CLI verb (a {@linkcode CommandSpec}), so a plugin can
extend `denext <command>` — not only the request/route/build seams. The command
is discovered when the CLI encounters an unknown verb in a project whose config
lists this plugin, and eagerly (under a time budget) when the CLI has to
enumerate every verb — `denext --help`, `denext completions <shell>`. A name that
collides with a built-in verb is ignored (core verbs always win). A name or alias
of one of Deno's code-running verbs (`run`, `x`, `eval`, `serve`, `compile`,
`install`, `uninstall`, `upgrade`, `task`) throws: `denext <name>` always means
Deno's there. Any other Deno verb's name (`bench`, `doc`, …) is dispatched to the
plugin only once `denext commands` has listed it. The stored spec
is a copy stamped with `source: "plugin"`, which groups it under "Project
commands" in the help table.

members.name: addDeployAdapter
members.doc:
Contribute a deploy adapter (see `denext/deploy`): `denext build` runs its `prepare` after
the build, with the deploy manifest, when `denext.config.ts` names no `deploy.adapter` of its
own, and `denext deploy` uses it. The first one a plugin contributes wins.

members.name: addDeployRoutes
members.doc:
Contribute the routes this plugin serves to the deploy manifest
(`.denext/deploy-manifest.json`'s `routes`), so a deploy adapter sees them: a router plugin's
pages (`"static"` when `denext export` writes them, else `"dynamic"`) and its endpoints
(`"route-handler"`). `source` is called when the manifest is collected (after `denext build`,
and by `denext deploy`), and its routes are sorted in with the App Router's.

Optional, so a plugin that calls it as `ctx.addDeployRoutes?.(…)` still runs on a host from
before it existed.

members.name: addDeployAssets
members.doc:
Contribute the files this plugin serves as they are to the deploy manifest
(`.denext/deploy-manifest.json`'s `assets`): a router plugin's client bundle under its own URL
prefix, each group with the `Cache-Control` the plugin sends (`immutable` when the names are
content-hashed). `source` is called when the manifest is collected; a group with no files is
left out.

Optional, so a plugin that calls it as `ctx.addDeployAssets?.(…)` still runs on a host from
before it existed.

members.name: addTeardown
members.doc:
Register a disposer to run when the server drains — the symmetric shutdown
for anything {@linkcode DenextPlugin.setup} opened (a file watcher, a
connection, a timer). Disposers run most-recently-registered first. Per-plugin
state itself needs no special seam: a handler/step/teardown registered inside
`setup` closes over `setup`'s scope, so they already share state.

members.name: servesRoutes
members.doc:
Declare that this plugin serves the app's pages from a route tree of its own (a Pages Router
`pages/` tree, a TanStack Start or React Router route config), so the app needs no `app/`
directory: `denext doctor` passes its "app directory" check naming the plugin, where it
otherwise fails a project without one. A plugin that only adds endpoints beside the app's
pages (an API, docs, auth, storage) does not call it, however many request handlers it adds.

Optional, so a plugin that calls it as `ctx.servesRoutes?.()` still runs on a host from
before it existed.

symbols.docFull:
Build the {@link ./adapter.ts | AuthAdapter} on Postgres: every method group (users,
accounts, verification tokens, credentials, API tokens, MFA, native app sessions, passkeys,
account deletion) plus a `sessions` store over the **same** client and an idempotent
`close()`.

Ids are `crypto.randomUUID()` unless the caller supplies one; emails are matched
case-insensitively and whitespace-trimmed, and a unique index refuses a second user on one
address. The tables are created by migrations on first use (see the module doc).

symbols.name: rateLimit
symbols.doc: Fixed-window rate limit per key: the (max+1)th request in a window fails with a 429 rate_limited envelope carrying retry-after (seconds) — before validation, so a flood never reaches a schema or the handler. The client identity is the socket peer, or the last x-forwarded-for hop only when the proxy is trusted (a forged header can't dodge it): the limiter's own trustForwardedHeaders when set, else the app's (trustForwardedHeaders / DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1, read per request). An IPv6 address counts against its /64.
symbols.docFull:
Fixed-window rate limit per key: the (max+1)th request in a window fails with a 429
`rate_limited` envelope carrying `retry-after` (seconds) — before validation, so a flood
never reaches a schema or the handler. The client identity is the socket peer, or the last
`x-forwarded-for` hop only when the proxy is trusted (a forged header can't dodge it): the
limiter's own `trustForwardedHeaders` when set, else the app's (`trustForwardedHeaders` /
`DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1`, read per request). An IPv6 address counts against its /64.

The default key is skipped — the request is not limited — when the client address is a
loopback, private, link-local or unique-local socket peer and no trusted forwarded hop names
the client (`clientIpForLimits()`'s rule): that peer is most likely a reverse proxy every
visitor shares, so one bucket would rate-limit the whole site. A warning says so once per
process. The app's `rateLimitLocalAddresses` counts such a peer by its own address instead,
and its `rateLimitHeader` (e.g. `cf-connecting-ip`) keys on the address the proxy names there
whenever a request carries one — both app-wide, whatever this limiter's own
`trustForwardedHeaders`. A custom `key` is always applied.

members.name: max
members.doc: Failed attempts allowed per key per window before a `429`. Default 5.

members.name: windowMs
members.doc: Window length in ms. Default 15 minutes.

members.name: keyGenerator
members.signature: keyGenerator?: (request: Request, credentials: Record<string, string>) => string
members.doc:
Derive the limiter key from the request + the submitted credentials. The default
combines the client IP (the socket peer; behind a proxy declared with
`AuthConfig.trustForwardedHeaders`, the last `x-forwarded-for` hop) with the
submitted identifier (`email` / `username` / `login` / `identifier`, lower-cased).
Override when your proxy uses another header or you want a coarser/finer key.

members.name: store
members.doc: A shared store (Redis, SQL, …) instead of the per-process in-memory default.

members.name: signin
members.doc:
Tune the **sign-in-start** limiter — the per-IP budget for `GET
{basePath}/signin/:provider`, which is counted on every hit rather than only on
failures. `max`/`windowMs`/`keyGenerator` above belong to the credentials limiter and
never apply here; `store` is shared by both (their keys are namespaced apart).

members.name: session
members.doc:
Tune the **session-read** limiter — the per-IP budget for `GET {basePath}/session`,
counted on every hit. Default 300 per minute, which is far above any sane
`SessionProvider` poll and still bounds an unauthenticated flood. Like `signin`, it
shares `store` and ignores `max`/`windowMs`/`keyGenerator`.

members.name: verification
members.doc:
Tune the **verification** limiter — outbound-token requests (password-reset,
email-verification, magic-link and one-time-code sends), counted on every request for an address whether or not
the address has an account, so a throttled unknown address answers exactly like a
throttled known one. The IP-wide bucket allows `IP_BUCKET_FACTOR` (10)× `max`. Shares
`store`; ignores the credentials `max`/`windowMs`/`keyGenerator`.

members.name: mfa
members.doc:
Tune the **MFA** limiter — second-factor attempts per user, plus an IP-wide bucket at
`IP_BUCKET_FACTOR` (10)× `max`. Shares `store`; ignores the credentials fields.

members.name: captcha
members.signature: captcha?: { max?: number; windowMs?: number } | false
members.doc:
Tune the **captcha** limiter — the per-IP budget spent on every captcha token denext is
about to send to the provider (denext's own endpoints and `/auth/v1` alike), BEFORE the
provider is called, so no unauthenticated request stream can drive unlimited verifier
calls. A missing or oversized token is refused without spending. `false` turns this one
budget off. Shares `store`; ignores the credentials fields. Skipped, like every per-IP
budget, for a loopback/private peer with no trusted proxy hop.

Inject Expo web's root style into the SPA shell's `<head>`:
`html,body,#root{height:100%;margin:0}` and `#root{display:flex}` (`#root` follows
`spa.rootId`). React Native's root view is `flex: 1` and needs a sized flex parent;
without it the app collapses to its content height and absolutely positioned overlays
cover the page. It comes before `spa.head`, so a rule there overrides it.

shim, which implements the package's API over `denext/mobile` and web APIs. A package
without a shim resolves normally. `false` resolves every `expo-*` package normally.

Which engine runs the app's lists. `"denext"` (the default): React Native's `FlatList`,

`@legendapp/list` (its React Native entry) run on denext's `VirtualList`, with the same
props and ref methods. `"library"`: each resolves to the real implementation.

members.doc:
Per-package switches for the community-package aliases. React Native mode resolves
popular React Native libraries whose native half a WebView lacks to denext
implementations (`react-native-webview` → an `<iframe>` WebView,
`react-native-keychain` → `denext/mobile`'s `secureStore`, `@react-navigation/native-stack`
→ `denext/navigation`'s stack, …: the list is `/docs/react-native`'s "Community packages"
table). Every alias is on by default; `{ "<package>": false }` resolves that package
normally again (`"react-native-svg-transformer": false` keeps `.svg` imports as asset URLs).

members.doc:
Build a React Native macOS or Windows app's web version: a bare `react-native` import in
the app's own source (not in node_modules) resolves as `react-native-macos` or
`react-native-windows` does in React Native mode (react-native-web plus that package's
additions: the desktop `View` props, `Flyout`, `Popup`, `DynamicColorMacOS`, …), as
Metro's platform resolution does for a desktop build. The app's source stays unchanged.
Unset, `react-native` is react-native-web and only an explicit
`react-native-macos` / `react-native-windows` import gets the additions.

shell gets an `@font-face` rule for each, and the files ship with the client. `denext
migrate --from expo` writes it from the app config.

components (`className` on every component), react-native-web's stylesheet gets uniwind's
layered one, and uniwind registers `light`, `dark` and `extraThemes` (the `extraThemes`
the app's Metro config passes to `withUniwindConfig`). Compile the app's Tailwind input
with `tailwind: { input, output }`. `false` turns it off.

members.name: onCaughtError
members.doc:
Invoked with the **raw** error each time an `error.tsx` boundary catches during
this render. A caught boundary renders its fallback and the render succeeds, so
the error would otherwise be swallowed — the caller uses this to report it to

cheap (defer any async reporting).

members.name: onHoleError
members.doc:
Invoked with the **raw** error each time a streamed Suspense hole throws and nothing
inside the hole catches it: the hole keeps its fallback in a response whose 200 status
already left, so the caller reports it to `onRequestError`. Keep it non-throwing.

as a hole the response streams after its payload, instead of awaiting it.

members.name: request
members.doc: The incoming request.

members.name: routes
members.doc:
The app's route manifest + module loader, for a runtime that reflects over the routes
while handling a request (the Remix compat's synthesized `ServerBuild`). Set by
`createApp`; absent outside an app (unit renders, export).

members.name: requestId
members.doc:
Correlation id for this request. Surfaced in the request log and the
server-side error log, and echoed as the `x-request-id` response header on an
error, so a client-visible 500 can be traced back to its logged detail. Honors
an inbound `x-request-id` only when the app trusts its fronting proxy
(`trustForwardedHeaders` / `DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1`, sanitized to safe token
characters); otherwise mints a fresh UUID.

members.name: signal
members.doc:
Per-request abort signal — fires on client disconnect or request timeout.
Thread it into outgoing `fetch()`es for cooperative cancellation. Set by the
request handler; absent when running outside a request.

members.name: timeoutMs
members.doc:
This request's deadline in ms from its start, when {@linkcode setRequestTimeout} replaced
the app's `requestTimeout` (`0`: none). Read by `createApp`'s timeout when it fires.

members.name: rearmTimeout
members.doc: Re-arms `createApp`'s timer for a new {@linkcode RequestContext.timeoutMs}.

members.name: holdDeadline
members.doc:
Stops `createApp`'s deadline clock until the returned release is called (see
{@linkcode holdRequestDeadline}); unset when the request has no deadline.

members.name: trustForwardedHeaders
members.doc:
Whether the app trusts `x-forwarded-for` for the client address — mirrors
{@linkcode AppConfig.trustForwardedHeaders}. Read by {@linkcode clientIp}; set by
`createApp` from the config. When unset (a direct handler call in a test), only the
socket peer is used.

members.name: limitPolicy
members.doc:
How per-address limits pick their address beyond {@linkcode RequestContext.trustForwardedHeaders}
— the app's `rateLimitHeader` / `rateLimitLocalAddresses`. Read by
{@linkcode clientIpForLimits}, `rateLimit()` and `denextAuth`'s per-IP budgets; set by
`createApp`. Unset: neither (a direct handler call in a test). `header` is lower-cased.

members.name: cors
members.doc:
The app-level CORS policy (`config.cors`), set by `createApp`. The native `denextAuth`
endpoints read it to answer an app WebView's origin; `null`/absent means no CORS.

members.name: desktopAppOrigin
members.doc:
The app's own Deno Desktop origin ({@linkcode AppConfig.desktopAppOrigin}), set by
`createApp`. `denextAuth`'s same-origin gate accepts an `Origin` exactly equal to it.

members.name: originAllowlist
members.doc:
The app's same-origin allowlist ({@linkcode AppConfig.allowedOrigins} and
{@linkcode AppConfig.canonicalOrigin}), set by `createApp`. The `csrf()` API middleware
applies the same rule Server Actions do with it.

members.name: outgoingHeaders
members.doc: Headers accumulated to attach to the response (e.g. Set-Cookie, loader-set headers).

members.name: renderPageForMethod
members.doc:
Set by a compat runtime's middleware (`denext/fresh`) that ran a page route's handler for a
method other than GET / HEAD and wants the page to render its result, as Fresh renders a
page for any method whose handler returns page data. Without it such a request to a page is
a 405.

members.name: cspTransform
members.doc:
Set by a compat runtime's middleware (`denext/fresh`'s `csp()`) to adjust this response's
Content-Security-Policy: called with the policy denext computed for the document (undefined
when `csp` is `"off"`), it returns the policy to send (undefined: none). It may also queue
headers on {@linkcode outgoingHeaders} (a report-only policy, `Reporting-Endpoints`).

members.name: localeNegotiated
members.doc:
Set when the request's locale was negotiated (`detectLocale`: the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie or
`Accept-Language`; `localeMiddleware`, next-intl's middleware): the response may differ per
visitor on the same URL, so `cdnCacheHeaders` never marks it public.

members.name: renderScope
members.doc: Per-request render collectors (signal state, `useServerInsertedHTML`) — see `render-scope.ts`.

members.name: cacheScope
members.doc:
The render's cache scope behind `cacheSignal()` (see {@linkcode renderCacheSignal}): created on the
first call, aborted when the render ends or the request is aborted.

members.name: cacheScopeEnded
members.doc: Set once the render's cache scope has ended ({@linkcode endCacheScope}).

members.name: routing
members.doc: Routing facts the pipeline resolved (`NextRequest.nextUrl.basePath` / `.locale` read them).

members.name: readonlyHeaders
members.doc: Memoized read-only view handed out by {@linkcode headers}.

members.name: responseStatus
members.doc:
An explicit response status a loader/action requested for this request (e.g. Remix
`data(value, { status })`). Applied by the request handler's `finalize` over the
render's own status. Absent on a normal render (keeps the render's status).

members.name: softNavBody
members.doc:
The parsed JSON body of a soft-navigation POST (a client soft nav that carries a payload
too large for request headers — e.g. the Remix `shouldRevalidate` prior-data echo). Opaque
to the core dispatch; the feature that sent it interprets it. Absent on normal requests.

members.name: slotState
members.doc:
Parallel-route slot state the client echoed on a soft navigation
(`x-denext-slot-state`): slot key → the pathname that slot last matched, so an
unmatched slot re-renders its previous content instead of `default.tsx`. See
`server/slot-state.ts`. Absent on a hard load.

members.name: renderedSlotState
members.doc: The slot state this render produced (shipped to the client in the nav/hydration data).

members.name: screenOptions
members.doc:
The rendered page's `export const screenOptions` (`denext/navigation`'s per-route stack
options), shipped to the client in the nav/hydration data. Absent when the page has none.

members.name: documentAttrs
members.signature: documentAttrs?: { html?: Record<string, unknown>; body?: Record<string, unknown> }
members.doc:
Attributes a root component put on ITS `<html>`/`<body>` (a root layout's
`<html lang="fr">`, a migrated Remix root's `<html className={theme}>`), merged onto the
real document tags by the assembler.

members.name: memo
members.doc: Per-request memoization store backing {@link cache}, keyed by function.

members.name: subRequestDepth
members.doc:
How many self-calls deep this request is (a typed-API batch item, or the typed client
called during SSR — see `server/sub-request.ts`). Absent for a client request.

members.name: postponedBy
members.doc:
A self-call's handler read the request it inherited (`cookies()`, `headers()`, or the
request's own headers) during a prerender: the dynamic API it postponed on. The caller's
render postpones on it too (`runSubRequest`), so the boundary around the call becomes a
per-request hole instead of baking the visitor's data into a shared shell.

members.name: usedDynamicApi
members.doc:
Set when the render read a dynamic request API (`cookies()`/`headers()`),
implying per-request output. The page cache checks this and refuses to cache
such a render even when the route opts in via `revalidate`.

members.name: renderStreamed
members.doc:
Dev-only render-mode telemetry for the first-party devtools glass-box
(`denext/devtools`). `renderStreamed` is set true just before a streamed response
is constructed; `renderCache` records this route's page-cache outcome. The
document renderer serializes them (with `usedDynamicApi`) into a dev-only
`#__denext_render_modes` JSON island the devtools panel reads. Ignored in
production (the island is emitted only when `__denextDev` is set).

members.name: renderCache
members.doc: This request's page-cache outcome (see {@link renderStreamed}).

members.name: segmentConfig
members.doc:
The effective route {@link SegmentConfig} for the page being rendered, set by
`buildPageContext` once the layout→page chain is merged. The dynamic-API guards
read it: `dynamic:"error"` makes `cookies()`/`headers()`/`connection()` throw,
and `dynamic:"force-static"` makes them return empty without marking the render
dynamic (so it caches). Absent outside a page render (e.g. a route handler).

members.name: compressOptOut
members.doc:
The served route opted out of response compression (`export const compress = false`)
on a path that does not resolve {@link segmentConfig} — an ISR cache hit. Read with
`segmentConfig.compress` by the response compressor (compress.ts).

members.name: collectedTags
members.doc:
Tags accrued from cached data read during this render (via
{@link unstable_cache}/{@link cachedFetch} `tags`). The page cache attaches
them to the stored render so {@link revalidateTag} can purge the page, not
just the underlying data. Populated lazily on first tagged read.

members.name: updatedTags
members.doc:
Tags a Server Action expired **this request** via `updateTag` (read-your-writes).
A same-request cache read whose entry carries one of these treats it as a miss and
recomputes, so the acting user sees their own write immediately. Also surfaced to
the client so its router can refresh the affected content.

members.name: refreshRequested
members.doc:
Set when a Server Action called `refresh()` — a request to re-fetch the
uncached data on the current route. Surfaced to the client in the action
response so its router refreshes (complements `updateTag`).

members.name: deferred
members.doc: Callbacks registered via {@link after}, drained after the response.

members.name: headersCommitted
members.doc:
Set once the response headers are committed — the streaming path sets it at its
first flush (see {@link beginStreamedBody}). From then on `cookies().set()`/`.delete()`
can't reach the response: dev throws, prod logs once and ignores the write.

members.name: bodyStreaming
members.doc:
True while a streamed body is still being produced: the pipeline leaves the
{@link after} drain to the stream's end instead of running it when the Response
object is created (a callback registered inside a streamed Suspense hole would
otherwise never run). Cleared by the `end` {@link beginStreamedBody} returns.

members.name: warnedCommittedCookies
members.doc: Guards the prod "cookies modified after the response started" log (once per request).

members.name: resourceHints
members.doc:
Serialized `<link>`/`<script>` resource hints emitted during SSR by
`preload`/`preinit`/`preconnect`/`prefetchDNS` (React's resource-hint APIs).
Merged into the document `<head>` by the page renderer. Populated lazily via
{@link addResourceHint}; deduped by exact tag string.

members.name: trackParamReads
members.doc:
Set by the request handler when `cacheKeyParams` narrows the ISR cache key, so
the render props' `searchParams` is wrapped to record which param names the
render actually read (see {@link trackSearchParamReads}). Off by default — the
normal render path is untouched unless the key is narrowed.

members.name: keyedParams
members.doc:
The `searchParams` names the narrowed ISR key keeps (`cacheKeyParams`), set with
{@link trackParamReads}. A read of any other name while a Cache Components shell
prerenders postpones (see {@link trackSearchParamReads}).

members.name: unkeyedShellRead
members.doc:
Set when a prerender read a `searchParams` name outside {@link keyedParams} without
postponing (inside a `use cache` body): the shell embeds a value its key does not
carry, so it must not be stored.

members.name: paramReads
members.doc:
The `searchParams` names read during this render, recorded only while
{@link trackParamReads} is set. The page cache dev-warns
({@link warnUnkeyedParamReads}) if a whole-body-cached render read a name the
narrowed key ignores — a value that would otherwise bleed across requests.

members.name: warnedUnkeyedParams
members.doc: Guards {@link warnUnkeyedParamReads} so the dev warning fires at most once.

symbols.docFull:
The correlation id for the current request — the value logged with the request and its
errors, and echoed as the `x-request-id` response header on an error. Honors an inbound
`x-request-id` only when the app trusts its proxy (`trustForwardedHeaders` /
`DENEXT_TRUST_PROXY=1`); otherwise it is a fresh UUID, so a client can't pick its own id.

symbols.docFull:
The current request's abort signal — fires on client disconnect or the request timeout.
Thread it into outgoing `fetch()`es (and any cancellable work) for cooperative
cancellation, so a client that navigates away actually reclaims the work.

Cancellation plumbing, not request data: reading it does **not** make the render dynamic.
Inside a `use cache` scope it is `undefined`: a cached fill is shared by single-flight
followers and background refreshes, so one client's disconnect must not abort work other
readers are waiting on. Also `undefined` outside denext's server loop.
symbols.returns: The abort signal, or undefined outside a request or inside a use cache scope.

symbols.name: requireAuth
symbols.signature: requireAuth(request: Request, options?: RequireAuthOptions): Promise<Response | null>
symbols.doc: Middleware guard: allow the request through when signed in, otherwise return a redirect to the sign-in page carrying a callbackUrl back to the target.
symbols.docFull:
Middleware guard: allow the request through when signed in, otherwise return a
redirect to the sign-in page carrying a `callbackUrl` back to the target.

Four checks, in order: no session → the sign-in page; a session still owing a second
factor → `pages.mfa` (or the sign-in page); `role` not held → the sign-in page with
`?error=forbidden`; then `callbacks.authorized({ session, request })` — `false` refuses
exactly like a missing session, and a returned `Response` is passed through verbatim.

A request that passes all four also slides the session's expiry forward when
`session.updateAge` is configured — the re-issued cookie is queued on the request and
attached to the response the pipeline finalizes, so "continue" still carries it.

Use in `middleware.ts` (matcher-gated):
```ts
export async function middleware(request: Request) {
  return await requireAuth(request); // returns a Response to redirect, or null to continue
}
export const config = { matcher: ["/dashboard/:path*"] };
```

symbols.name: requireBearer
symbols.signature: requireBearer(config: AuthConfig, options?: RequireBearerOptions): ApiMiddleware<object, BearerContext>
symbols.doc: Require a valid bearer API token (denext auth): verifies Authorization: Bearer tok_…, loads the token's user, and extends the handler's context with BearerContext — or fails with a 401 unauthorized envelope before any schema runs. A valid token that lacks the required scope or role fails with 403 forbidden instead, so "who are you" stays distinguishable from "may you".
symbols.docFull:
Require a valid bearer API token (denext auth): verifies `Authorization: Bearer tok_…`,
loads the token's user, and extends the handler's context with
{@link BearerContext} — or fails with a `401 unauthorized` envelope before any schema
runs. A valid token that lacks the required `scope` or `role` fails with `403 forbidden`
instead, so "who are you" stays distinguishable from "may you".

```ts
// lib/auth.ts
export const authed = createApi().use(requireBearer(authConfig, { scope: "pets:write" }));
// app/api/pets/route.ts
export const POST = authed.define({ body: NewPet }, ({ body, ctx }) => add(ctx.user.id, body));
```

The middleware is tagged with `documentsSecurity(…, [{ bearerAuth: [] }])`, so
`@denext/openapi` marks every endpoint that applies it as secured — declare the matching
`securitySchemes: { bearerAuth: … }` once in the plugin options for the Authorize button.

Bearer authentication **never sets a cookie** and never slides a session forward. It is
also never accepted on the `{basePath}/*` auth endpoints — minting and revoking tokens
requires the interactive session, so a stolen token can't mint more of itself.

with a 401 `unauthorized` envelope before any schema runs. With `role`, a signed-in caller

symbols.name: resetPassword
symbols.signature: resetPassword(config: AuthConfig, input: { email: string; token: string; password: string }): Promise<ResetPasswordResult>
symbols.doc: Redeem a password-reset token and set a new password: the configured hasher hashes it, adapter.setCredential stores it, every passkey of the user is removed, and every server-side session and bearer API token is revoked — a reset is how an owner takes an account back, so nothing a thief set up with a stolen session (a passkey registered from it included) survives it. Fires passwordReset (after sessionRevoked).
symbols.docFull:
Redeem a password-reset token and set a new password: the configured `hasher` hashes it,
`adapter.setCredential` stores it, every passkey of the user is removed, and every
server-side session and bearer API token is revoked — a reset is how an owner takes an
account back, so nothing a thief set up with a stolen session (a passkey registered from it
included) survives it. Fires `passwordReset` (after `sessionRevoked`).

The password is checked (8–1024 characters) **before** the token is touched, so a
refused password leaves the link usable.

symbols.signature: revalidateTag(tag: string, profile?: string | CacheLifeProfile): Promise<void>
symbols.doc: Invalidate every cached data entry and page carrying tag.
symbols.docFull:
Invalidate every cached data entry and page carrying `tag`.

- **`revalidateTag(tag)`** (single arg) hard-purges the entries — the original
  (Next.js-deprecated but still supported) form.
- **`revalidateTag(tag, profile)`** soft-expires them with stale-while-revalidate
  timing from the `cacheLife` `profile` (a name like `"max"`/`"hours"` or an inline
  `{ stale, revalidate, expire }`): entries are served **stale** while refreshed in
  the background, matching Next.js 16. Stores without soft-expire support
  ({@link CacheStore.expireByTag}) fall back to a hard purge.

With the in-memory default the change is applied synchronously; with an **async
store you should `await` the returned promise**. Inside a request it is also
drained via the deferred queue.

params.name: profile
params.doc: Optional cacheLife profile for stale-while-revalidate behavior.

symbols.name: revokeApiToken
symbols.signature: revokeApiToken(config: AuthConfig, id: string, options: { userId?: string }): Promise<boolean>
symbols.doc: Revoke a token by id — it stops authenticating immediately and can never be revived. Revoking an unknown (or already revoked) id is a no-op, not an error, and fires nothing; an actual revocation fires apiTokenRevoked (reason: "revoked").

params.name: options

symbols.name: revokeSession
symbols.doc: Revoke one session by id, so its cookie stops authenticating from the next read — "sign out this device". Fires the sessionRevoked event.
symbols.docFull:
Revoke one session by id, so its cookie stops authenticating from the next read — "sign out
this device". Fires the `sessionRevoked` event.

- **Store-backed** (`denextAuth({ sessionStore })`): `sessionId` is the session's
  {@link AuthSession.sessionId}; its record is deleted from the store.
- **Stateless** (no `sessionStore`): `sessionId` is the session's own
  {@link AuthSession.sid}; it goes on the auth adapter's revocation list (`revokeSids`) for the
  larger of `session.maxLifetime` and 400 days (so a lifetime raised later can't outlive it),
  and every read of a stateless session checks that list from then on (`isSidRevoked`, at most
  once per request). Until an app first revokes a session this way its reads make no such
  query. Needs an adapter with the list: `sqliteAuthAdapter`, `postgresAuthAdapter`,
  `inMemoryAuthAdapter` (one process) or `backendAuthAdapter()`; throws with one that lacks it
  (an Auth.js adapter) or with none.

{@link currentSessionId} gives the current request's id; never send it to the browser.

symbols.name: safeFetch
symbols.signature: safeFetch: (url: string | URL, opts?: SafeFetchOptions) => Promise<Response>
symbols.doc: SSRF-safe fetch for **untrusted / user-supplied URLs** (link previews, "import from URL", avatar-by-URL, webhooks). Use it instead of fetch() whenever the destination is influenced by an end user.
symbols.docFull:
SSRF-safe `fetch` for **untrusted / user-supplied URLs** (link previews, "import
from URL", avatar-by-URL, webhooks). Use it instead of `fetch()` whenever the
destination is influenced by an end user.

It resolves the host and refuses the request if any resolved address is
loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/multicast, then connects to that pinned IP with
the original Host/SNI (closing DNS rebinding). Redirects are followed only after
re-validating each hop; the download is time- and size-bounded. Pass `signal`
(from an `AbortController`) to cancel; it is combined with `timeoutMs`.

A refused or failed request throws {@linkcode SafeFetchError} (inspect `.code`);
a real HTTP response — including 4xx/5xx from the origin — is returned for you to
handle. Do **not** use this to reach your own internal services — that's what
`fetch`/`cachedFetch` are for.

symbols.name: safeRedirectLocation
symbols.doc: Make a redirect Location safe against open redirects. An explicit http(s):// absolute URL is preserved (a deliberately-configured external redirect); anything else is forced to a single-slash, same-origin path so a protocol-relative (//host) or backslash (/\host) prefix — which browsers resolve cross-origin — cannot escape the current origin.
symbols.docFull:
Make a redirect `Location` safe against open redirects. An explicit
`http(s)://` absolute URL is preserved (a deliberately-configured external
redirect); anything else is forced to a single-slash, same-origin path so a
protocol-relative (`//host`) or backslash (`/\host`) prefix — which browsers
resolve cross-origin — cannot escape the current origin.

SEC-L3 — the absolute-URL passthrough is deliberate but unconstrained: a fully
qualified `http(s)://…` value is returned as-is (no host allowlist), so it is an
open redirect if built from untrusted input. Only pass an absolute URL that is
statically configured or otherwise trusted; for anything derived from the request
(query/path/header), pass a PATH so it is pinned to the current origin, or
validate the host against your own allowlist before calling this.

A SAML 2.0 identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, ADFS, Keycloak, …) on

symbols.doc: Define a server action. Give it a **stable, explicit id** (unique per app) so the client stub and the server handler agree across the boundary.
symbols.docFull:
Define a server action. Give it a **stable, explicit id** (unique per app) so
the client stub and the server handler agree across the boundary.

On the server the returned function runs `handler` directly and registers it
for RPC dispatch. In the browser it returns a stub that POSTs the arguments to
the action endpoint and resolves with the JSON result.

The handler runs with the request's async context, so it may read
`cookies()`/`headers()`, call `revalidatePath`/`revalidateTag`, or `redirect()`.
It **must** authorize and validate its own input — registration alone exposes
it to any same-origin caller.

params.name: id
params.doc: A stable, app-unique identifier for this action.

symbols.returns: A ServerActionRef usable as a <form action> or called directly.

symbols.docFull: A reference to a server action: callable, and tagged with its stable id.

members.name: secret
members.doc:
HMAC signing secret — at least 32 chars (shorter warns in development and throws
under `NODE_ENV`/`DENEXT_ENV=production`). Pass an **array** to rotate: every secret
verifies, the first signs — so deploy the new secret first, then retire the old one. Use a
long random value (e.g. `crypto.randomUUID()` + more), kept out of source.

members.name: cookieName
members.doc: Cookie name. Default `"denext_session"`.

members.name: hostPrefix
members.doc:
Origin-lock the session cookie with the `__Host-` name prefix (RFC 6265bis).
The browser then binds the cookie to the exact origin: it must be `Secure`,
`Path=/`, and carry **no `Domain`**, and a sibling subdomain can neither read
nor overwrite it — closing subdomain session-fixation/shadowing. denext (via
the cookie layer) guarantees those attributes, so no other config is needed;
it works on `http://localhost` too (browsers treat localhost as secure), but a
non-localhost plain-HTTP origin can't store a `Secure` cookie.

**Recommended for new apps.** Off by default because enabling it renames the
cookie to `__Host-<name>`, which invalidates sessions issued under the
unprefixed name (users are logged out once, on the upgrade). No-op if
`cookieName` already begins with `__Host-`.

members.name: maxAge
members.doc: Session lifetime in seconds. Default 7 days.

members.name: sameSite
members.doc: Cookie `SameSite`. Default `"Lax"`. `"None"` always sets `Secure`, which browsers require.

members.name: path
members.doc: Cookie `Path`. Default `"/"`. Forced to `"/"` when `hostPrefix` is set.

symbols.doc: Where store-backed sessions live. Every method may be sync or async; get must return only an **unexpired** session (treat expiresAt in the past as a miss).

Where store-backed sessions live. Every method may be sync or async; `get` must

members.signature: create(id: string, session: AuthSession): void | Promise<void>
members.doc: Persist `session` under the (random, unguessable) `id`.

members.name: update
members.signature: update?(id: string, session: AuthSession): boolean | Promise<boolean>
members.doc:
Optional, but **required for sliding expiry** (`session.updateAge`): rewrite an
EXISTING record in place — write-only-if-present. It must NOT create a row: the
whole point is that a session revoked between the read and the refresh stays
revoked instead of being resurrected with a fresh lifetime by an upsert.

A store that doesn't implement it simply never slides its sessions forward
({@link ../auth/session.ts | refreshIfStale} returns the session untouched and
warns once), which is safe — the session still expires on its original schedule.
members.returns: true when a live row was rewritten; false when id is unknown, revoked or expired (nothing was written).

symbols.name: SpaConfig
symbols.doc: SPA-mode settings (mode: "spa"). denext bundles SpaConfig.entry as a single client-side-rendered app, wraps it in a generated HTML shell, and serves that shell for every navigation (history-API fallback) — no app/ directory, no SSR/Flight. The entry module mounts the app itself (a side-effect import, like a Vite main.tsx calling createRoot(...).render(...)), so denext stays out of the mount: bring your own router (TanStack, etc.) and data layer.
symbols.docFull:
SPA-mode settings (`mode: "spa"`). denext bundles {@link SpaConfig.entry} as a
single client-side-rendered app, wraps it in a generated HTML shell, and serves
that shell for every navigation (history-API fallback) — no `app/` directory, no
SSR/Flight. The entry module mounts the app itself (a side-effect import, like a
Vite `main.tsx` calling `createRoot(...).render(...)`), so denext stays out of the
mount: bring your own router (TanStack, etc.) and data layer.

members.name: entry
members.doc:
Client entry module that mounts the app, relative to the project root
(e.g. `"./src/main.tsx"`). It is imported for its side effects — it is
expected to create a root and render into `#${rootId}` on load.

members.name: rootId
members.doc: Element id the generated shell exposes for the app to mount into. Default `"root"`.

members.name: title
members.doc: `<title>` for the generated shell. Default `"denext app"`.

members.name: head
members.doc:
Extra raw HTML injected into the shell `<head>` (meta tags, preconnect links, …).
A `<meta name="viewport">` here replaces the shell's default
(`width=device-width, initial-scale=1`) — e.g. `viewport-fit=cover` for iOS safe areas.

members.name: loading
members.doc:
Raw HTML rendered INSIDE the mount element (`#${rootId}`) in the generated shell — the boot placeholder shown before the client bundle loads and renders. The framework does not touch it; the app's first render (createRoot/hydrateRoot) replaces `#root`'s children, clearing it. Use it to paint instantly instead of a blank page: a themed background (pair with a pre-paint script in {@link head}), a logo splash, or a spinner — the same role a Vite/CRA `index.html` fills with markup inside `
…
`. `denext migrate --from vite` carries the source `index.html`'s `#root` content here. Setting it together with {@link shell} is a config error.

members.name: shell
members.doc:
A prerendered, adoptable static shell: a component server-rendered into `#${rootId}` at
build, export and dev, so the page paints the app's real layout (with the app's CSS) and
its fields accept typing before the client bundle has loaded. The app then renders
off-screen and replaces the shell in one commit, carrying over what was typed. Replaces
{@link loading}. See {@link SpaShellConfig}.

members.name: lang
members.doc: `<html lang>` value for the generated shell. Default `"en"`.

members.name: env
members.doc:
Compile-time `import.meta.env` values (the SPA analogue of a Vite `define`
block). Each `{ KEY: "value" }` replaces `import.meta.env.KEY` with the literal
`"value"` at build time — the way a Vite app reads `import.meta.env.VITE_*`.
Only applied when the app builds through the next-compat (esbuild) pipeline
(i.e. it uses npm React); a denext-native SPA has no `import.meta.env`.

members.name: csp
members.doc:
Content-Security-Policy for the generated shell. A client-only React SPA
(Vite/CRA and denext alike) ships no CSP by default — it's the app's/host's
call — so this is **opt-in**:
- unset / `"off"` — no CSP (default).
- `"strict"` — denext's strict policy (`default-src 'self'`, `script-src 'self'`,
  `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`, `img/font 'self' data:`, and
  `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'` so React `style={{}}` keeps working).
- a {@link CspSetting} object — that strict policy plus your global opt-ins
  (e.g. `{ connectSrc: ["https://api.example.com"] }` for your API host).

Emitted as a `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` in the shell so it
applies for `export` (any static host), `start`, and `dev` alike. `frame-ancestors`
is header-only (ignored in `<meta>`); clickjacking is covered by the always-on
`X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`. Set a header at your edge for `frame-ancestors`.

members.name: proxy
members.doc:
Reverse-proxy selected path prefixes to a separate backend while serving the SPA
(`denext start` in `mode:"spa"`, and the `deno desktop` runtime). Mirrors a Vite
dev server's `server.proxy`: the client talks to its own origin and denext relays
matched requests — HTTP and WebSocket — to the backend. Omit for a backend-less SPA.

members.name: precompress
members.doc:
Write a gzip `.gz` sibling next to each compressible client asset at `build` and
`export`, so `denext start` serves `Content-Encoding: gzip` with no per-request CPU.
Default `true`. Set `false` when the export is bundled into a native shell such as
Capacitor, whose iOS/Android webview loads files from the app bundle and never requests
the `.gz` variants, to keep them out of the bundle.

members.name: ota
members.doc:
Stamp the static export for over-the-air UI updates: `denext export` writes
`_denext/ota.json` (every file's path, SHA-256 and size, plus a `version` hashed over
them) into the export directory as its last step. A Capacitor shell with the
`DenextOta` plugin (`denext mobile add-ota`) reads the bundled copy to know which UI it
ships, and `checkForUiUpdate` from `denext/mobile` compares a server's copy against it.
Default `false`. `*.gz` siblings are never listed. When the `DENEXT_OTA_SIGNING_KEY` env var
holds a PKCS#8 PEM (`denext ota keygen`), the manifest is also signed.

Write a Vite-shaped build manifest, `.vite/manifest.json`, into the static export: one
entry per content-hashed client file (`"_denext/client/chunk-AB12CD34.js": { "file":
"_denext/client/chunk-AB12CD34.js" }`, under {@link assetsDir} when set), the shape Vite's
`build.manifest` writes. A server written for a Vite build reads it to learn which files
are safe to serve as `immutable`. The entry `index.js` and `index.css` keep their names
across builds and are not listed, nor is any `public/` file. Default `false`.

members.name: assetsDir
members.doc:
Where the client output (entry, stylesheet, split chunks, imported assets) is served and
exported, as Vite's `build.assetsDir`: `"assets"` serves it from `/assets/` and writes it to
`out/assets/`, with content-hashed files named `name-HASH.ext` (an 8-character hash), the
shape a server written for a Vite build expects. A `public/` file at the same path is served
behind the build's. Unset, the client lives under `/_denext/client/`. A directory under
`_denext`, `.well-known` or `.vite` is refused. `denext migrate` sets it from a Vite app's
`build.assetsDir` (`"assets"` by default).

each route file's `component` (and loader, error/pending/not-found components) into its own
chunk loaded on navigation, as `@tanstack/router-plugin`'s `autoCodeSplitting` does under
Vite. Applies on the esbuild path (npm React / `compatibilityMode`); `denext dev` bundles
routes unsplit. `denext migrate` carries it from a `vite.config` that sets it.

members.name: icon
members.doc:
Path to the app icon (relative to the project root, e.g. `"./assets/icon.png"` —
point it anywhere, regardless of name or location). **Overrides icon
auto-detection.** A **PNG is used verbatim** (supply a finished 1024² master already
shaped for macOS — the app's own icon set is the right source); a JPEG/WebP is
composed into the macOS template; an undecodable format (`.ico`/`.icns`) is refused
with a message and the build falls back to auto-detection. When unset, denext
auto-detects a web icon (`apple-touch-icon`, a named `icon`/`logo`, `favicon.png`)
and, because those are small/full-bleed, composes it into Apple's macOS template
(centered in the ~824px safe area of a 1024² canvas) so it isn't oversized. Either
way the result is written to `desktop-icon.png` at build time.

The `deno task desktop` command carries `--icon desktop-icon.png` only when an app
icon was detected at migrate time. If your app had one then, editing this and
rebuilding is enough — no re-migration. If migrate found no icon (so the task has no
`--icon`), re-run `denext migrate --desktop` after setting this so the flag is wired.

symbols.docFull:
Reverse-proxy configuration for SPA serving — the SPA analogue of a Vite dev
server's `server.proxy`. The client talks to its own origin and denext relays

members.name: prefixes
members.doc:
Path prefixes forwarded to {@link target}, matched against the start of the
request pathname — a prefix matches the exact path and any sub-path (e.g. `/api`
matches `/api` and `/api/users`). Everything else is served from the SPA export.

members.name: target
members.doc:
Backend origin matched requests are forwarded to (e.g. `"http://127.0.0.1:3773"`).
HTTP is relayed via `fetch` (cookies passed through, `Set-Cookie` `Domain`/`Secure`
stripped so they bind to the proxy origin over http); a WebSocket upgrade is
bridged to the backend with the request `Cookie` forwarded on the handshake.

This is a **desktop/dev convenience** for reaching a *local* backend, not a
production reverse proxy — the target must be loopback unless
{@link allowNonLoopback} is set (at which point the security implications of
running an open reverse proxy are yours).

symbols.doc: The prerendered static shell under SpaConfig.shell.
symbols.docFull:
The prerendered static shell under {@link SpaConfig.shell}.

`component` is server-rendered into the mount element (marked `data-denext-shell`) with the
app's stylesheet linked in `<head>`, so first paint has the final layout and fonts. Mark each
field the user may type into before the app starts (`<textarea>`, `<input>`,
`contenteditable`) with `data-denext-shell-key="<key>"`: an inline script records its text,
selection, focus and scroll as the user types. When the app is ready (see {@link readyOn})
it replaces the shell in one commit, and an app field with the same key gets the state: an
`<input>` / `<textarea>` is filled in and focused by denext; anything else (an editor) reads it
with `useShellHandoff(key)` / `consumeShellHandoff(key)` from `denext`.

members.name: component
members.doc:
The shell component's module, relative to the project root (`"./src/AppShell.tsx"`); its
default export is rendered. It must be pure: plain elements and the app's class names, no
app runtime (no router, store or data), no stylesheet import (the app's own CSS applies). A
platform file beside it (`AppShell.desktop.tsx`, `AppShell.ios.tsx`) is used for that
export target.

members.name: bootScript

A module bundled into one classic script and inlined before the shell markup (with a CSP
hash under `spa.csp`): it runs before first paint, to set `<html>` classes or CSS variables
from `localStorage` (a saved theme) so the shell paints in them.

members.name: platforms
members.doc:
The export targets that carry the shell (`["macos", "windows", "linux"]` for a desktop-only
shell). Default: every target. A target without it gets the plain empty mount element.

members.name: readyOn
members.doc:
When the app replaces the shell. `"first-settled-commit"` (default): its first commit with
no Suspense boundary showing a fallback. `"shellReady"`: when the app calls `shellReady()`
(from `denext`), e.g. once its editor has mounted. `shellReady()` also swaps early under the
default.

The longest the shell is kept once the app has started, in milliseconds: the app replaces
it then even without a ready signal. Default `5000`.

symbols.name: spendMfaAttempt
symbols.signature: spendMfaAttempt(config: AuthConfig, input: { userId: string; request?: Request }): Promise<MfaAttemptResult>
symbols.doc: Spend one second-factor attempt from the user's MFA budget — the one the POST {basePath}/mfa* endpoints spend — before a Server Action checks a code with verifySecondFactor or confirmTotp, which spend nothing themselves. Every attempt counts, right or wrong, so a correct guess never resets the count. The per-user budget is rateLimit.mfa (5 per 5 minutes by default), and the client IP's bucket counts too when a request is in scope. Pass the config you passed to denextAuth() so the endpoints and your actions share one budget.

Run `fn` in a transaction: COMMIT when it settles, ROLLBACK (and rethrow) when it throws.
An array `fn` returns is awaited as a whole (`Promise.all`), as `Deno.SQL` and postgres.js
do: `begin(tx => [tx\`…\`, tx\`…\`])` lets the driver pipeline the statements and COMMIT.

rethrow) when it throws. Optional: `Deno.SQL` and {@linkcode fromPostgresJs} have it; a
nested transaction needs it.

re-listening after a lost connection; `onlisten` runs once subscribed and again after each
reconnect (notifications sent while it was down are lost). Optional: `Deno.SQL` and
{@linkcode fromPostgresJs} have it; realtime features need it.
